data.title: arXiv moving from Cornell servers to Google Cloud
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary:
arXiv，作为康奈尔大学的一部分，正在招聘多个软件工程职位，包括普通软件工程师、DevOps专家和科学家/软件开发员。这些职位均为康奈尔大学员工，需具备在美国工作的合法权利，不提供签证 sponsorship。工作地点主要在纽约市的康奈尔科技校区，但也可能提供混合或远程工作选项。

当前，arXiv 正在进行将其服务迁移至谷歌云的“Cloud Edition”项目，旨在提升可扩展性和现代化基础设施。具体任务包括替换旧的Perl和PHP代码、实现异步处理、容器化服务、改进监控和日志系统，以及建立可靠的CI/CD管道。

招聘的职位要求具备多种编程语言和环境的经验，特别是Web开发和SQL。DevOps专家将专注于现代化开发运维体系，使用基础设施即代码原则和Google Cloud工具。科学家/软件开发员需有科学研究背景和arXiv使用经验，代表科研社区的利益。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Arxiv迁移到Google Cloud Platform (GCP) 的决策及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **商业化和资金支持的担忧**：
   - [x_may] 认为此次迁移可能是技术公司将资本支出转为运营支出的常见决策，并质疑GCP是否会承担部分费用，或者全部由康奈尔大学支付。推测GCP可能通过提供服务换取合作机会，并预测Google未来可能会发布自我宣传的博客文章。
   - [tokai] 反对让Google参与，认为科学出版已经被私人企业掌控，建立国际学术图书馆联盟才是正确方向。
   - [kevinventullo] 提出可以通过设立非营利组织来解决资金问题，并表示愿意捐款支持arXiv。

• **招聘和技能问题**：
   - [andyjohnson0] 认为迁移的动机可能是技能短缺和招聘问题，并指出如果是因为美国政府的压力，那么Google可能是一个更安全的选择，但arXiv仍可能受到恶意行为者的资金干扰。
   - [gcr] 提到康奈尔大学目前处于招聘冻结状态，这些职位可能无法填补。

• **技术架构和成本担忧**：
   - [dig1] 担心迁移到GCP会导致简单性和稳定性丧失，并带来高昂的月度费用，对服务质量表示怀疑。
   - [sppfly] 关心谁将支付GCP的服务费用，以及arXiv是否仍将免费提供服务。

补充讨论：
• **地缘政治和访问限制的担忧**：
   - [darkoob12] 担心像伊朗这样的国家会被封锁，因为互联网越来越多地由美国公司控制，他们可以决定哪些内容和人群可以访问。

• **对联邦政府行动的担忧**：
   - [perihelions] 提到联邦政府与康奈尔大学的矛盾，担心康奈尔大学可能因为政府行为而无法继续运营arXiv。

• **用户体验的改善**：
   - [Daviey] 对迁移表示欢迎，因为可以更方便地下载论文，而无需伪装用户代理。

• **其他推测和历史背景**：
   - [kiproping] 提到arXiv的历史和曾经发生的小风波，并猜测其创始人Ginsparg是否即将退休并交出控制权。
   - [harywilke] 提供了有关arXiv与开放学术合作伙伴关系的历史链接，指出此迁移计划早在2023年3月就开始了。

• **对论文处理的影响**：
   - [ilynd] 提到自己的论文提交被延迟，可能与此次迁移有关。

争议焦点：
• 是否应该让Google参与arXiv的运营，反对者认为这会导致学术资源进一步商业化，支持者认为这可能是解决资金和技能短缺问题的必要措施。

43726640.article_content:
Careers at arXiv
arXiv is part of Cornell Tech, the graduate campus and research center of Cornell University. All arXiv employees are Cornell University employees.
Positions at arXiv are
staff positions with benefits (endowed)
.
Visa sponsorship is not available. You must already possess the legal right to work in the US.
arXiv is headquartered at the
Cornell Tech campus on Roosevelt Island in New York City
. When hiring, there is a strong preference for candidates who can report to work at that location, but hybrid and/or remote work may be an option.
Software development
We are already underway on the arXiv CE ("Cloud Edition") project. This is a project to re-home all arXiv services from VMs at Cornell to a cloud provider (
Google Cloud
). There are a number of reasons for this transition, including improving arXiv's scalability while modernizing our infrastructure. This will not be a simple port of the existing arXiv code base because this project will:
replace the portion of our backends still written in perl and PHP
re-architect our article processing to be fully asynchronous, and provide better insight into the processing workflows
containerize all, or nearly all arXiv services so we can deploy via Kubernetes or services like
Google Cloud Run
improve our monitoring and logging facilities so we can more quickly identify and manage production issues with arxiv.org
create a robust CI/CD pipeline to give us more confidence that changes we deploy will not cause services to regress
The cloud transition is a pre-requisite to modernizing arXiv as a service. The modernization will enable:
- arXiv to expand the subject areas that we cover
- improve the metadata we collect and make available for articles, adding fields that the research community has requested such as funder identification
- deal with the problem of ambiguous author identities
- improve accessibility to support users with impairments, particularly visual impairments
- improve usability for the entire arXiv community
We have three SWE openings, one general and two specialized
Software Engineer
This person should be a software generalist, who can work in a variety of environments, programming languages, frontend and backend. Should have web development and SQL experience.
Software Engineer IV
(Software Engineer)
DevOps Specialist
We are looking for a developer with Cloud DevOps experience to lead the effort of modernizing our devops system so we can efficiently, reliably, and securely deploy new code, using Infrastructure as code principles. This task will likely involve a fair amount of automation via
gitops
, as well as Google Cloud Platform tools. The devops lead will also put in place a robust CI/CD pipeline, and may also be asked to help fill in test cases.
DevOps Software Engineer
Scientist/Software Developer
We're looking for someone with serious software development skills who has also used arXiv for scientific research, and preferably someone who has authored arXiv submissions. We expect this person to represent and be an advocate for the interests of all scientists, within the arXiv software development team (no pressure!). We believe there are lots of you scientists-turned-software-developers out there. Please apply!
Software Engineer Scientist
43726640.article_summary:
arXiv，作为康奈尔大学的一部分，正在招聘多个软件工程职位，包括普通软件工程师、DevOps专家和科学家/软件开发员。这些职位均为康奈尔大学员工，需具备在美国工作的合法权利，不提供签证 sponsorship。工作地点主要在纽约市的康奈尔科技校区，但也可能提供混合或远程工作选项。

当前，arXiv 正在进行将其服务迁移至谷歌云的“Cloud Edition”项目，旨在提升可扩展性和现代化基础设施。具体任务包括替换旧的Perl和PHP代码、实现异步处理、容器化服务、改进监控和日志系统，以及建立可靠的CI/CD管道。

招聘的职位要求具备多种编程语言和环境的经验，特别是Web开发和SQL。DevOps专家将专注于现代化开发运维体系，使用基础设施即代码原则和Google Cloud工具。科学家/软件开发员需有科学研究背景和arXiv使用经验，代表科研社区的利益。

主要讨论点：[关于人口统计数据和生育意愿的讨论]

不同观点：
• [seydor的观点] 认为发达国家在人口下降问题上更加严重，尤其是南欧国家，但这些国家缺乏详细的调查和有效的公共政策。他批评现有的政策大多是粗略、表面且民粹主义的，且往往失败。

• [Cyphase的观点] 没有直接参与人口统计或政策的讨论，而是提供了一个PDF链接，帮助那些不想启用 cookies 的人访问相关数据。这一评论更侧重于分享资源，而非发表立场。

• [PaulKeeble的观点] 对数据中体现的生育意愿下降趋势表示关注，但他认为关键问题在于理解人们不愿生育的原因。他指出，尽管数据展示了生育障碍的细分，但不愿意生育的原因可能更加复杂，不是简单的“不想”。

补充讨论：
• [seydor] 提到了南欧国家在人口趋势调查和政策上的不足，并对此表示失望，暗示需要更深入的研究和更有效的政策。

• [PaulKeeble] 强调了对不愿意生育原因的深入分析需求，表明当前的数据可能尚未完全捕捉到问题的复杂性。

争议焦点：
• 人口统计数据的透明度和深度：seydor批评南欧国家在人口趋势调查上的不足。
• 生育意愿的复杂性：PaulKeeble认为不愿生育的原因需要更详细的分析，而不仅仅是数据展示。

这些观点共同构成了对当前人口统计和公共政策有效性的多角度讨论。

data.title: Multipaint: Draw pictures with color limitations of 8-bit and 16-bit platforms
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: Multipaint 2025是一款绘图工具，支持多种8位和16位计算机平台的色彩限制，如Commodore 64、ZX Spectrum、Amiga和Atari ST等。它提供多种绘图工具，包括色彩冲突模拟、剪切笔刷、网格、30步撤销等功能，并支持直接导出可执行文件和源代码。最新版本2025.1修复了"最近文件"功能的崩溃问题，并改进了文件管理功能，如通过"File->Recent"访问最近文件，"File->Workstage"用于递增文件名。此外，新增"Other->Stamp"功能可快速保存PNG文件，适用于工作阶段和延时摄影。对于Mac用户，由于代码签名问题，应用可能无法直接运行，建议使用"Nothing Works"方法或Docker解决方案。根据系统不同，可能需要升级Java至OpenJDK 17或更高版本。

不同观点：

• [VyseofArcadia] 关注软件在颜色和分辨率限制上的表现，尤其是是否能够通过编程技巧增加颜色数量。这反映了对技术细节和潜在功能扩展的关注。

• [waltbosz] 对复古游戏美学进入创意软件领域表示兴趣，并提出是否可以将其扩展到其他软件类别，比如旧式字处理软件的用户体验。这引发了对不同类型软件中复古风格应用的讨论。

43699431.article_content:
Multipaint 2025
Multipaint 2025 (Version 3.2.2025)
With Multipaint, you can draw pictures with the color limitations of some typical 8-bit and 16-bit computer platforms.
Some of the screen formats supported are Commodore 64, Commodore Plus/4, Commodore Vic-20, ZX Spectrum, MSX, Amstrad CPC, Sinclair QL, Commodore Amiga and Atari ST.
Multipaint features common drawing tools, color clash emulation, cut brushes, dither patterns, grid / snap, 30-step undo, spare page, magnify modes, direct executable export, export as source, import/export in native formats and much more.
Looking at the recent file window.
Where the new menu items are.
Latest version :
Multipaint 2025.1
fixes a bug in the "recent file" function, which caused MP to crash eventually. Removing entries from data/recentfiles.txt can also improve the situation.
For updating, it may be useful to copy the data/recentfiles.txt and paste it to the data folder of the new install. However if you already experienced crashes, better get rid of it.
Preview window can be forced on top (use "t" key while focused on the preview window).
Multipaint 2025
is the tenth major release of Multipaint. The version introduces more tools for handling files, meant to help managing your projects and producing workstage images.
You can now access previously saved files from a menu item
File->Recent
. One-directional exports (such as .prg or .tap) are not added, as they cannot be loaded back.
You can increment the number in your filename with
File->Workstage
, e.g. picture1.bin will become picture2.bin. Take care of your naming convention, sid6581.bin will become sid6582.bin :)
From
Other->Stamp
you can instantly save a png to the current file's path, named as
path/filename.ext_YYYY_MMDD_HHMMSS.png
. This can be also useful for workstages, but also for creating timelapses. (Multipaint does not make videos.) The shortcut for this action is the * key. This is not the same as SAVE-ing the file, and does not affect the current filename.
Taken together, it is now easier to have a single project/single folder approach, where all the relevant files to one image are held in the same folder.
An older VIC-20 export note, but it checks out: There are different exports for unexpanded VICs and with expansion. With unexpanded VIC exports, you need to provide a
10 LOAD "image",8,1
loader or use PuCrunch.
See also:
A blog post with some background for the 2024 version.
Download and running the app
Mac OS
: Note that because of code signing and notarization issues, the application is very unlikely to run, but will be reported as damaged. I'm not going to pay for an Apple Developer license at this point. If the packaged app doesn't run, you can still choose the "Nothing Works" route below.
Choose your path:
The transition to Processing 4 is not yet forced, because it might require many to upgrade their Java. But it may be needed especially for really recent Apple M1 or Windows computers. P4 is now very explicit that it requires OpenJDK 17 or higher. (See examples below.)
–I just want to upgrade, my Multipaint from 2023 works just fine:
Download Multipaint application for Windows/Linux/Mac (zip)
Processing 3 app, needs the same Java "as before."
–I have a recent OS/Computer/CPU, the previous Multipaint no longer works:
Download Multipaint application for Windows/Linux/Mac (zip)
Processing 4 app, Requires OpenJDK 17 or higher.
–Nothing works, I'll use the Processing Development Environment and run/export the source:
Get Processing from
here
, if you don't have it.
Download Multipaint Processing 3/4 sketch, v. 3.2.2025
(zip, no manuals)
Place the extracted multipaint folder inside your sketchbook folder, run Processing, open and run the sketch. Use File/Export Application in the Processing Development Environment to create a self-running app.
Notes
about supported platforms for the PDE in the P4 wiki.
For
MacOS
users, you can also try a docker-based solution from Toni Nurminen. (
GitHub link
).
Java and the JRE
As Multipaint is written in
Processing
, it should run in Windows, Mac OS X and Linux 32/64 bit systems. For running the application, you need the
Java Runtime Environment.
It may turn out you already have it. For some systems, installing something like Arduino might also install a version without further hassle.
If an error message demands an exact version of Java, I cannot guarantee it actually means what it says. It may also drop out of the app silently. Running it from command line may provide some information. I don't have that much control over the matter.
Examples with Processing 4
Using the "P4" marked zip, this will require OpenJDK 17 or higher.
Here are a few experiences, some steps may require you to enable system permissions.
Also, installing over older version of Java may need a different process.
Windows 11Pro
Running the windows-amd64 version, the system alerts it needs Java Runtime Environment 17.
This took me to Adoptium's website, suggesting the download of Eclipse Temurin

data.title: Startup Exercise: What can't be solved with money? (2011)
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了金钱无法解决的商业关键要素，强调在寻求投资时，创业者应明确哪些问题能通过金钱解决，哪些不能。金钱可以加速执行，如写更多代码、增加营销投入等，但无法买到创意、团队、市场洞察和关键知识等。特别指出，优秀的团队和权威的建立（如社交媒体影响力）无法单靠金钱实现。创业者应展示自己在金钱无法解决领域的能力，如学习、适应和改进，并提前识别和规划这些方面，以获得投资者信任。如果没有核心团队或明确计划，不应急于筹集资金。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于资金在研究和项目中的作用

不同观点：
• [mnky9800n] 认为，尽管无限制的资金支持理想化上很吸引人，但在申请研究经费时，明确描述经费能解决的问题以及团队带来的限制是明智的做法。这种观点强调了资金对研究项目的实际约束和导向作用，指出在申请资金时需要清晰地界定研究范围和目标。

• [ltbarcly3] 则认为，重要的方面如产品直觉、工程 talent 以及动机和 alignment 等问题，不是仅仅依靠金钱就能解决的。这一观点挑战了资金万能的想法，强调了人才和内在驱动等非金钱因素的重要性。

补充讨论：
• [mnky9800n] 的评论集中在资金申请的实际操作和策略上，提出限制和明确目标的重要性。
• [ltbarcly3] 的评论更侧重于强调非金钱因素的关键作用，认为一些核心问题无法通过资金解决。
• 争议的焦点在于资金在解决问题中的实际效用。一方认为资金能有效推动项目进展，但需要明确规划；另一方则认为资金并不能解决所有重要问题，人才和动机等内在因素更具决定性。

43727138.article_content:
Startup Exercise: What canât be solved with money?
by Jason Cohen on March 21, 2011
What can’t be solved with money, are the most valuable things.
source
When pitching an investor, one of the key things you need to communicate is how
the important problems facing your business can be solved with money
, because money is what they are providing.
Even if youâre not raising money this is a useful exercise, because if youâre good at the things money
canât
buy, youâll remain competitive even when
confronted by a well-funded competitor
.
So, itâs useful to separate the aspects of your business that could be improved with money alone, from what instead requires time, attention, intelligence, and even
luck
.
Team
Finding good people is almost impossible. I have this blog, a nice Twitter following, attention in my local community, and social âfavorsâ I can call in, and itâs still almost impossible. And the thing about great people is they always have options: Existing job, other excellent offers, the freedom to not work for a while, etc..
If someone handed me a million dollars it wouldnât help me find an awesome person; theyâre just scarce.
Once I find someone, however, then money helps a lot, because I could satisfy large salary requirements, handle relocation, provide a signing bonus, lease a car, or whatever else is necessary to make money ânot the issue.â
So if youâre raising money and you donât have your team assembled, the investor knows that handing you $200,000 wonât fix that. Whereas if you have the team, but theyâre working only in their spare time because day jobs pay the mortgages, thatâs a good reason to raise money.
Marketing
Marketing of most sorts can be solved with money. Money means you can
spray ads everywhere
. Money means you can
try 20 campaigns
even if
most utterly fail
. Money means you can try 50 titles/descriptions/landing pages through AdWords until you find one that converts decently. Money means you can
fund a Freemium offering
.
One big exception is anything that requires
authority
, like blogging and social media. You canât buy authority. You canât buy that
kind
of attention, where people listen because they want to listen, not because theyâre interrupted, where they interact with you because they respect your opinion and enjoy your style.
Social media marketers have already beat this point to death. But if your business requires the modern âtell-your-friendsâ social-media-style punditry, youâll have to
do that without money
. If itâs just a matter of pouring more marketing dollars in the top so you can crank out more revenue in the bottom, thatâs a machine investors like to invest in.
And so forth
You see the pattern, so
letâs accelerate
; what can money solve?
Writing more code, faster, yes.
Knowing
what
to write, no.
Acquiring more leads, yes. Know how to convert them, no.
A
prettier website
, yes. What text to put on the website, no.
Leeway to make mistakes, yes. Philosophy of learning and
using mistakes
to improve, no.
A QA team to improve quality, yes. Knowing when a bug isnât important enough to prevent shipping, no.
Time to
outlive a recession
, yes. Making something people
want to buy
even during a recession, no.
The pattern: Concepts, behaviors, knowledge, and process cannot be fabricated with money, and possibly cannot even be accelerated. Once you know what to do or, more likely, you know how to learn quickly, then money becomes an accelerant.
Even more briefly using the
Explore vs Execute modalities
: Execution can be solved with money; exploration cannot.
source
Now thereforeâ¦
How can you use this principle to raise money?
Emphasize how spending money will improve specific things which, today, are broken or missing
only
because money is lacking.
Show proof of your ability to master the things money cannot buyâyour ability to learn, change, and improve.
For those things money can accelerate, and for which youâve spent a teeny amount of money, show how well youâve done with that. Itâs easy to imagine more money bringing more results.
For those things money canât solve and which you havenât mastered, bring it up before the investors do. And have a plan, proving youâre self-aware and thorough. If you donât have a clear, plausible plan, donât raise money yet.
Specifically, donât raise money if you havenât assembled the core team.
Let me make point #2 tangible.
I cannot count the times Iâve heard someone proclaim how adaptable they are. âIâm in love with A/B testing.â âIâm not afraid to admit when Iâm wrong.â âI listen to my customers.â âIâm a big fan of Eric Ries.â
Yeah,
you and 60,000 other people
. Iâm supposed to be impressed?
Since everyone and their dog is now an expert in Lean Startup, you need to
demonstrate
, not regurgitate platitudes. Tell me about how and why your pitch changed when you
vetted your idea with potential customers
. Walk me through a
screenshot
o

data.title: Curiosity rover finds large carbonate deposits on Mars
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: NASA's Curiosity rover has discovered large carbon deposits on Mars, indicating the past presence of a carbon cycle, which is crucial for understanding the planet's ancient climate and potential habitability. The discovery of siderite, an iron carbonate, in sulfate-rich layers of Gale Crater suggests that Mars once had a thicker atmosphere rich in carbon dioxide, supporting liquid water. As Mars' atmosphere thinned, the carbon dioxide likely transformed into rock, contributing to the planet's current cold, dry state. This finding, published in *Science*, brings scientists closer to determining whether Mars could have supported life. The research also has implications for understanding climate change on Earth, as studying carbon sequestration on Mars can inform efforts to mitigate carbon emissions.

April 17, 2025
The GIST
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's

and

Curiosity rover finds large carbon deposits on Mars
by
University of Calgary
NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover sees its tracks receding into the distance at a site nicknamed “Ubajara” on April 30, 2023. This site is where Curiosity made the discovery of siderite, a mineral that may help explain the fate of the planet’s thicker ancient atmosphere. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS
Research from NASA's Curiosity rover has found evidence of a carbon cycle on ancient Mars, bringing scientists closer to an answer on whether the red planet was ever capable of supporting life.
Lead author Dr. Ben Tutolo, Ph.D., an associate professor with the Department of Earth, Energy and Environment in the Faculty of Science at the University of Calgary, is a participating scientist on the NASA Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover team.
The team is working to understand climate transitions and habitability on ancient Mars as Curiosity explores Gale Crater.
The paper,
published
in the journal
Science
, reveals that data from three of Curiosity's drill sites had siderite, an iron carbonate material, within sulfate-rich layers of Mount Sharp in Gale Crater.
"The discovery of large carbon deposits in Gale Crater represents both a surprising and important breakthrough in our understanding of the geologic and atmospheric evolution of Mars," says Tutolo.
Reaching the strata, he says, was a long-term goal of the Mars Science Laboratory mission.
Ben Tutolo, associate professor in the Department of Earth, Energy and Environment in the Faculty of Science at the University of Calgary, is the lead researcher on a paper about Mars. Tutolo is a participating scientist on the NASA Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover team. Credit: Riley Brandt/University of Calgary
"The abundance of highly soluble salts in these rocks and similar deposits mapped over much of Mars has been used as evidence of the 'great drying' of Mars during its dramatic shift from a warm and wet early Mars to its current, cold and dry state," says Tutolo.
Sedimentary carbonate has long been predicted to have formed under the CO
2
-rich ancient Martian atmosphere, but Tutolo says identifications had previously been sparse.
NASA's Curiosity rover landed on Mars on Aug. 5, 2012, and has
traveled more than 34 kilometers
on the Martian surface.
The discovery of carbonate suggests that the atmosphere contained enough
carbon dioxide
to support
liquid water
existing on the planet's surface. As the atmosphere thinned, the carbon dioxide transformed into rock form.
NASA says future missions and analysis of other sulfate-rich areas on Mars could confirm the findings and help to better understand the planet's early history and how it transformed as its atmosphere was lost.
Tutolo says scientists are ultimately trying to determine whether Mars was ever capable of supporting life—and the latest paper brings them closer to an answer.
"It tells us that the planet was habitable and that the models for habitability are correct," he says.
"The broader implications are the planet was habitable up until this time, but then, as the CO
2
that had been warming the planet started to precipitate as siderite, it likely impacted Mars' ability to stay warm.
"The question looking forward is how much of this CO
2
from the atmosphere was actually sequestered? Was that potentially a reason we began to lose habitability?"
The latest research, he says, fits with his ongoing work on Earth—trying to turn anthropogenic CO
2
into carbonates as a climate change solution.
"Learning about the mechanisms of making these minerals on Mars helps us to better understand how we can do it here," he says. "Studying the collapse of Mars' warm and wet early days also tells us that habitability is a very fragile thing."
Tutolo says it's clear that small changes in atmospheric CO
2
can lead to huge changes in the ability of the planet to harbor life.
"The most remarkable thing about Earth is that it's habitable and it has been for at least four billion years," he adds. "Something happened to Mars that didn't happen to Earth."

data.title: AMP and why emails are not (and should never be) interactive
data.author: maguay
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Google尝试通过AMP技术让电子邮件变得互动，但遭遇广泛抵制。文章回顾了AMP的起源，最初用于加速移动网页加载，通过提供搜索排名优势等激励措施获得了一定采用，但也引发了对控制权和开放网络的担忧。当Google将AMP引入电子邮件，试图让用户直接在邮件中完成操作（如预订酒店、回复文档评论）时，遭到质疑，因为传统电子邮件以其简单、可靠和去中心化的特性著称。文章指出，电子邮件的魅力在于其跨平台兼容性和无需特定格式，而互动性可能破坏这种简约和可靠性。最终，Google的尝试被视为对开放网络的威胁，未获广泛接受。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AMPEmail和AMP技术的不同观点和争议

不同观点：
• Nifty3929认为，电子邮件作为记录应当是自我完备且不可变的，不应通过外部链接引用动态信息，以保证其长期可参考性。
• room271支持AMP的技术选择，认为其简化了开发并提升了性能，但反对其市场和政治上的垄断问题。他还提到AMP的技术理念在其他项目中仍然有价值。
• ingvar77支持AMP在特定场景下的应用（如确认、批准、动态信息等），并认为传统电子邮件应保持不变，允许用户自行选择是否包含动态内容。
• faust201指出，AMP在减少数据使用方面对资源有限的用户有益，尽管在富用户群体中存在垄断等问题。
• h1fra提到因SEO压力不得不采用AMP，但最终对结果不满，认为AMP对互联网整体有害。
• hughw调侃Google以往尝试替代电子邮件（如GoogleWave）失败的经历，暗示对AMP的失败并不意外。
• account-5庆幸AMP在电子邮件中的应用未能普及，并表达对AMP网站的主动回避态度。
• nottorp对由大公司（如Google、Cloudflare）主导的技术标准持怀疑态度，认为应尽量避免使用。
• epc回忆Netscape曾在90年代尝试动态电子邮件失败的案例，指出历史上类似尝试并不成功。
• _Algernon_批评AMP未能实现其主要设计目标——提高速度，认为其失败是显而易见的。
• 0xbadcafebee提出用Slack等现代工具替代电子邮件和传统聊天工具，主张建立开放标准以实现互操作性。
• ChrisArchitect认为AMP电子邮件未获得广泛 adoption，并指出HTML电子邮件通过标准化和现代客户端改善了体验。
• gregable为AMP辩护，指出对AMP在搜索排名和CDN缓存等方面的误解，并认为AMP在技术上有其价值，但承认其市场和政治上的争议。

补充讨论：
• 对AMP的争议焦点在于其技术实现与市场垄断问题之间的矛盾。
• 不同用户对电子邮件的本质功能有不同看法，一部分人强调不可变性和长期可参考性，另一部分人则接受动态内容和交互功能。
• 历史上的类似技术尝试（如GoogleWave、Netscape的动态电子邮件）提供了对AMP失败背景的理解。
• 对大公司主导的技术标准的信任问题也是讨论的重要方面。
• 对未来电子邮件替代方案的探讨，如Slack等现代工具的标准化为通信工具的发展提供了新的思路。

AMP and why emails are not (and should never be) interactive.
Google tried to reinvent email. Everyone said no.
“Email has largely stayed the same,”
wrote Gmail product manager Aakash Shaney
in 2019, while the web rapidly evolved around it.
No more. Google’s AMP for email meant “your emails can stay up to date” and “you can easily take action directly from the message itself.”
Four years earlier, the search giant had come for the mobile web with AMP—accreted mobile pages. Devs would code mobile versions of their site using AMP libraries, host them in Google’s CDN, and reap the benefits of near-instant load times and preferential placement in Google search results.
And now they were coming for your emails, dangling the benefits of a modernized messaging experience where you could book flights and hotels, respond to meeting invites and Google Docs comments, all from the comfort of your inbox.
“Who would ever want this?”
asked @waste_monk on Hacker News
. “We are living in hell.”
Dante's inbox
Yet the road to hell is paved with good intentions, as they say. That, and more than a little hubris.
On the web, AMP had gained grudging adoption through carrots and sticks. Build an AMP site, and you’d get
preferential placement in search results
, a grey lightning bolt near your site’s name in search results, and a near-zero latency page load from Google’s CDN—all carrots. “We are here to make the web great again,”
said Google’s vice president of news, Richard Gingras
in 2015, only months after Donald Trump brought that phrase into the vernacular. Google assumed publishers the world over would happily rewrite their mobile sites to the search giant’s whims.
The implicit stick, though, was that without an AMP page, your site wouldn’t rank as highly as it may have previously. And with
over 89% of global search volume
, when Google asks web publishers to jump, they say how high.
There were always issues with AMP. It brought back the dynamics of the mobile versus the desktop web, for one. Instead of the same web for everyone, you now had one page on mobile, another page on desktop—exactly what responsive web design had been fighting against ever since the iPhone brought a desktop-class browser to mobile. And, more critically, it lessened your control over your site.
AMP required allowing any AMP CDN to cache your pages. Visitors might be served your page from a Google domain instead of your own, or the ad tech and other scripts on your site might be incapable of running on your AMP site (handily, it seemed, for Google, who might prefer you to use their ad tech instead).
It was all enough that, over the coming years,
Google would come under two antitrust lawsuits
that referenced AMP as part of what the US Justice Department saw as Google’s attempt to monopolize online advertising and the web in general.
AMP libraries
themselves were open-source. And you could offer a competing AMP CDN;
Microsoft’s Bing did
, for one. But web developers viewed AMP with suspicion from the onset, as much due to the coercion as anything. “It’s a threat to the open web,” as
@ImprobableValue summed up
the prevailing opinion on Reddit.
And then Google brought AMP to email.
What if email was interactive?
Emails has always moved at its own, slower pace. The first email was sent twenty years before the first web page was published, and to this day, plain text emails without HTML are still considered compliant
internet messages
.
As Ray Tomlinson, who implemented and sent the first email from ARPANET in 1971
said about adding formatting to email
: “That’s too complicated: we just want to send messages to people.”
That, for better or worse, has been the ethos of email. It’s why every email message, today, should include both an HTML and plain text version, why you can email anyone and trust that they can read your message. It’s one of the remaining decentralized parts of modern communications, one where
Gmail supports only 152 of the 301 email HTML and CSS features
yet your messages still typically look fine.
Email’s great because “No company owns it. It works reliably and as intended on every platform, every operating system, every device. That’s a rarity today and a hell of a valuable one, ”
said TechCrunch’s Devin Coldewey
.
And here came Google, recommending everyone change how they write emails.
AMP email used the same frameworks as AMP on the web, with a
scaled-down set of components
. Some new stuff: AMP-form to gather info, AMP-autocomplete to suggest search and filter results, AMP-carousel to showcase said results. Some older stuff, rewritten: AMP-image to “replace the HTML5 img tag” and lazy-load images, AMP-anim to “manage an animated image, typically a gif,” and AMP-timeago for fuzzy timestamps.
It all worked, in Gmail, Yahoo! Mail, and (inexplicably) Mail.ru. Launch partner OYO Rooms let you browse hotel listings and reviews from emails.
Booking.com
let you flip through room photos—and change your

• faust201指出，AMP在减少数据使用方面对资源有限的用户有益，尽管在富用户群体中存在垄断等问题。
• h1fra提到因SEO压力不得不采用AMP，但最终对结果不满，认为AMP对互联网整体有害。
• hughw调侃Google以往尝试替代电子邮件（如GoogleWave）失败的经历，暗示对AMP的失败并不意外。
• account-5庆幸AMP在电子邮件中的应用未能普及，并表达对AMP网站的主动回避态度。
• nottorp对由大公司（如Google、Cloudflare）主导的技术标准持怀疑态度，认为应尽量避免使用。
• epc回忆Netscape曾在90年代尝试动态电子邮件失败的案例，指出历史上类似尝试并不成功。
• _Algernon_批评AMP未能实现其主要设计目标——提高速度，认为其失败是显而易见的。
• 0xbadcafebee提出用Slack等现代工具替代电子邮件和传统聊天工具，主张建立开放标准以实现互操作性。
• ChrisArchitect认为AMP电子邮件未获得广泛 adoption，并指出HTML电子邮件通过标准化和现代客户端改善了体验。
• gregable为AMP辩护，指出对AMP在搜索排名和CDN缓存等方面的误解，并认为AMP在技术上有其价值，但承认其市场和政治上的争议。

补充讨论：
• 对AMP的争议焦点在于其技术实现与市场垄断问题之间的矛盾。
• 不同用户对电子邮件的本质功能有不同看法，一部分人强调不可变性和长期可参考性，另一部分人则接受动态内容和交互功能。
• 历史上的类似技术尝试（如GoogleWave、Netscape的动态电子邮件）提供了对AMP失败背景的理解。
• 对大公司主导的技术标准的信任问题也是讨论的重要方面。
• 对未来电子邮件替代方案的探讨，如Slack等现代工具的标准化为通信工具的发展提供了新的思路。

data.title: All-in-Memory Stochastic Computing Using ReRAM
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种基于ReRAM的全内存随机计算（All-in-Memory Stochastic Computing）方法，以应对嵌入式和边缘设备对低功耗高效计算的需求。传统随机计算（SC）依赖于随机比特流（SBS）进行近似运算，但生成这些比特流通常消耗大量功耗和面积。本文利用ReRAM器件的特性，实现了在同一位置生成SBS、执行SC操作以及将SBS转换回二进制数的全流程。尽管ReRAM单元的可靠性较低，SC的容错性有效弥补了这一缺陷。实验结果显示，该方法在吞吐量和能耗方面较现有方案有显著改进，吞吐量提升1.39至2.16倍，能耗降低1.15至2.8倍，同时在图像处理任务中的图像质量仅下降约5%。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对IRAM的商业成功性、内存控制器的简化以及在多核CPU中增加RAM芯片的趋势的讨论。

不同观点：
• [anon6362] 质疑当前的项目是否只是对IRAM的更多步骤的重复。IRAM项目是否在商业上取得成功存在疑问，因为没有明显的证据显示其商业化成果。

• [anon6362] 提出是否存在一种趋势，通过在多核CPU中增加更多的RAM芯片来简化或消除内存控制器。他认为SoC（系统级芯片）的发展方向是包含固定数量的RAM。

补充讨论：
• [anon6362] 对IRAM项目的有效性和其在商业领域的应用提出质疑，特别是其是否真正带来了实际的商业价值。

• 关于内存控制器的讨论中，[anon6362] 提到了一种技术趋势，即通过在CPU中集成更多RAM芯片来简化系统设计，而不是依赖复杂的内存控制器。这暗示了一种可能的技术发展方向，旨在提高系统效率和集成度。

• 关于SoC的评论指出，当前的设计趋势似乎更倾向于将固定数量的RAM直接集成到芯片中，这可能反映了行业内对简化设计和提高性能的需求。

争议焦点：IRAM项目的商业成功与否及其在现代计算中的应用价值是主要争议点。此外，关于内存控制器简化与RAM芯片集成的技术路径也存在不同的看法和潜在的技术路线分歧。

Title:
All-in-Memory Stochastic Computing using ReRAM
Authors:
João Paulo C. de Lima

M. Hassan Najafi
,

View a PDF of the paper titled All-in-Memory Stochastic Computing using ReRAM, by Jo\~ao Paulo C. de Lima and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
As the demand for efficient, low-power computing in embedded and edge devices grows, traditional computing methods are becoming less effective for handling complex tasks. Stochastic computing (SC) offers a promising alternative by approximating complex arithmetic operations, such as addition and multiplication, using simple bitwise operations, like majority or AND, on random bit-streams. While SC operations are inherently fault-tolerant, their accuracy largely depends on the length and quality of the stochastic bit-streams (SBS). These bit-streams are typically generated by CMOS-based stochastic bit-stream generators that consume over 80% of the SC system's power and area. Current SC solutions focus on optimizing the logic gates but often neglect the high cost of moving the bit-streams between memory and processor. This work leverages the physics of emerging ReRAM devices to implement the entire SC flow in place: (1) generating low-cost true random numbers and SBSs, (2) conducting SC operations, and (3) converting SBSs back to binary. Considering the low reliability of ReRAM cells, we demonstrate how SC's robustness to errors copes with ReRAM's variability. Our evaluation shows significant improvements in throughput (1.39x, 2.16x) and energy consumption (1.15x, 2.8x) over state-of-the-art (CMOS- and ReRAM-based) solutions, respectively, with an average image quality drop of 5% across multiple SBS lengths and image processing tasks.

data.title: Using CAA Records with Namecheap
data.author: aaronmdjones
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了作者作为一个小型IRC网络的管理员，在使用Let's Encrypt证书和修改CAA记录时遇到的困难。尽管CAA记录和相关标准（如RFC 6844和RFC 8657）已存在多年，但DNS注册服务商Namecheap的系统却不支持正确输入这些记录，甚至连其客服也不熟悉CAA记录的操作。作者试图修改CAA记录以限制只有Let's Encrypt可以为其域名颁发证书，但Namecheap的系统报错，且客服最初未能理解问题。这反映了DNS注册服务商对其核心业务相关标准缺乏了解和支持的问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DNS管理和相关工具、服务的评价

不同观点：
• **[stop50]** 认为使用自建的DNS服务器（如PowerDNS）更为可靠，因为基于Web界面的DNS管理工具往往缺少某些记录类型或者在将记录传递给DNS服务器之前试图解析它们，导致问题。该用户强调自建服务器在功能上的完整性和自主控制的重要性。

• **[aaronmdjones]** 对事件的反应则是从内容创作的角度出发，计划撰写一篇博客来讨论此事件。该用户并没有直接对DNS管理方式发表看法，而是关注如何利用事件本身作为素材，暗示其对技术事件的传播和讨论感兴趣。

• **[popcalc]** 推荐了Infomaniak，认为这是一家拥有出色客户支持的罕见大型域名注册商。虽然没有直接讨论DNS管理的技术细节，但该用户强调了服务质量和客户支持在选择注册商时的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Web界面的DNS管理工具的可靠性和功能性。Stop50明确指出这些工具存在不足，特别是缺少记录类型和提前解析的问题。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是用户对服务质量的评价，比如popcalc对Infomaniak客户支持的积极评价，这表明在选择DNS相关服务时，客户支持也是一个重要的考虑因素。

• 最后，aaronmdjones的角度提供了一种不同于技术细节讨论的元层次讨论，即将技术事件转化为内容创作的机会。

43725616.article_content:
I'm getting tired of having to explain to
DNS registrars
(and even a
DNS registry
, once) how
DNS
works -- knowing this is literally their entire job, and yet this will be my sixth time doing so. But first, some context.
I am the principal administrator of a small
IRC
network. All of our
TLS
-related services use certificates from
LetsEncrypt
, the free and automated Certificate Authority created by the
ISRG
in the wake of the
Snowden revelations of mass unwarranted surveillance
.
Further work by ISRG and the
IETF
in this area includes
RFC 7258 (Pervasive Monitoring Is an Attack)
, which describes the reasonable belief that designing future application protocols to resist this mass surveillance is a Very Good Idea, and
RFC 8555 (Automatic Certificate Management Environment)
, which laid the framework for the process of requesting and installing TLS certificates to become entirely automated, resulting in the mass adoption of effortless HTTPS for all kinds of websites, big and small. This was basically the protocol that people were already using to interact with LetsEncrypt, but it had yet to be standardised. There were some changes, but this is not relevant to this blog post. The publication of this standard allowed other CAs to integrate with this ecosystem with confidence.
The IETF had also realised by this point that permitting any CA to issue certificates for any domain is a Very Bad Idea, so they had also published
RFC 6844 (DNS Certification Authority Authorization Resource Record)
, which is a standard that specifies a DNS record that domain name owners can create to restrict which CAs are allowed to issue certificates for it. This has since been superseded by
RFC 8659 (DNS Certification Authority Authorization Resource Record)
, but that is irrelevant for the purposes of this blog post for reasons I will get into.
For several years now, we have had a CAA record permitting only LetsEncrypt to issue certificates for our domain. However, it was a blanket CAA record, meaning that any LetsEncrypt account could request certificates for any name under our domain name. This is also less than ideal, because anyone can create a LetsEncrypt account in approximately 5 seconds, without supplying or verifying any personal information. To this end, I sought to modify our CAA records to use the
accounturi
and
validationmethods
parameters introduced by
RFC 8657 (Certification Authority Authorization Record Extensions for Account URI and Automatic Certificate Management Environment Method Binding)
.
It is important to note that this RFC only describes the specific naming and meaning of these two parameters; it does not introduce support for the parameters themselves. Parameter support has existed since RFC 6844, published over TWELVE years ago.
Context over, this is where my woes begin.
I login to Namecheap's domain administration interface in order to add some new CAA records. As soon as I type the very first semicolon following the CA issuer domain, it errors out, saying that this is an invalid record. The situation does not improve when I add a parameter (even though the syntax described by RFC 6844 does not require a parameter after a semicolon):
So, I reached out to Namecheap Support. This should be a very simple process, right?
From: Aaron Jones <redacted>
To: support@namecheap.com
Subject: Unable to modify CAA records
Date: Thu, 17 Apr 2025 05:47:17 +0000
Hello.
I write to enquire as to when your DNS records management interface
will properly support CAA records (introduced by RFC 6844 in
January 2013).
I am unable to add any parameters to the "issue" property as prescribed
by section 5.2 and documented at https://letsencrypt.org/docs/caa/ -
your interface insists that these perfectly valid records are anything
but, and the save button does not work.
I am attaching example screenshots.
Regards,
--
Aaron Jones
Network Administrator
The reply arrives approximately 20 minutes later (fantastic), but it is immediately off to an ominous start:
From: Namecheap Domains Support Team <domainsupport@namecheap.com>
Subject: Unable to modify CAA records
Date: Thu, 17 Apr 2025 06:08:49 +0000
Hello,
Thank you for contacting our Namecheap support team!
Unfortunately, the .asc extension is not supported here, so we
can't deal with such files. Supported extensions for chats and
emails: .ca-bundle, .cer, .crt, .csv, .doc, .docx, .eml, .jpeg,
.jpg, .key, .mov, mp4, .p12, .p7b, .p7c, .p7s, .pdf, .pem, .pfx,
.png, .txt, .wav, .xls, .xlsx, .zip.
As for the screenshots, the field marked in red seems to have an
incorrect value. In order for us to check the case further, we
need some additional details. Please specify:
1) Your Namecheap username
2) The Support PIN
3) CAA records in full form that you need to set up
4) Domains in question
We are looking forward to your reply.
-
Best regards,
Namecheap Team
Easy enough. Their ticketing system doesn't understand OpenPGP email signatures, a standard introduced almost 24 years ago by
RFC 315

data.title: CVE fallout: The splintering of the standard vulnerability tracking system
data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了常见漏洞与暴露（CVE）系统的分裂问题。由于美国政府一度中止对管理CVE的非营利组织MITRE的资助，导致CVE的未来充满不确定性。尽管最后一刻恢复了11个月的资金支持，欧洲已开始推出自己的漏洞数据库（EUVD），以减少对美国系统的依赖。同时，全球CVE分配系统（GCVE）和一个新的CVE基金会也相继出现。专家担心，多个漏洞追踪系统可能导致不一致，影响全球安全响应。文章强调了统一漏洞标识系统的重要性，以避免混乱和提高应对效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特朗普作为关键脆弱性与CVE资金合同到期的问题

不同观点：
• 观点一：关注特朗普作为国家安全的关键脆弱性。部分讨论者引用了文章标题和链接内容，强调特朗普的存在可能对国家安全构成威胁，尤其是在合同资金即将到期的情况下。他们认为，特朗普的政治影响力可能影响CVE（Countering Violent Extremism）项目的持续性，从而削弱国家应对极端主义的能力。

• 观点二：质疑文章和链接的相关性及可信度。一些讨论者对文章的来源和内容持怀疑态度，认为文章可能存在偏见或缺乏实质性证据。他们指出，需要更详细和可靠的信息来支持“特朗普作为关键脆弱性”这一论点。

• 观点三：讨论CVE项目资金到期的实际影响。部分讨论者更关注CVE项目本身的有效性和资金到期可能带来的实际影响。他们认为，不论特朗普的影响如何，CVE项目的资金问题是一个需要优先解决的政策问题，因为该项目对防止极端主义至关重要。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于特朗普的政治角色与国家安全项目的潜在联系。部分讨论者认为这是政治话题而非实际安全问题，而另一些人则认为两者间存在直接关联。

• 对文章和信息来源的信任度也是讨论中的一个重要方面，一些讨论者呼吁更严谨的信息来源和证据支持。

• 还有讨论者提到，政治领导人的更替可能对国家安全政策和项目产生广泛影响，而不仅仅局限于特朗普个人。

43726927.article_content:
CSO
5
CVE fallout: The splintering of the standard vulnerability tracking system has begun
5
MITRE, EUVD, GCVE … WTF?
Jessica Lyons
Fri 18 Apr 2025
//
09:54 UTC
Comment
The splintering of the global system for identifying and tracking security bugs in technology products has begun.
Earlier this week, the widely used Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (
CVE
) program faced doom as the US government
discontinued
funding for MITRE, the non-profit that operates the program. Uncle Sam U-turned at the
very last minute
, and promised another 11 months of cash to keep the program going.
Meanwhile, the EU is rolling its own.
The European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA) developed and maintains this alternative, which is known as the
EUVD
, or the European Union Vulnerability Database. The EU mandated its creation under the Network and Information Security 2 Directive, and ENISA
announced
it last June.
The EUVD is similar to the US government's
NVD
, or National Vulnerability Database, in that it organizes disclosed bugs by their CVE-assigned unique ID, documents their impact, and links to advisories and patches.
Interestingly, the Euro database also uses its
own EUVD IDs
to track security bugs as well as CVE-managed identifiers and GSD IDs, the latter of which are issued by the (what appears to be now-defunct)
Global Security Database
operated by the Cloud Security Alliance.
Although the EUVD has been gestating for nearly a year, the uncertainty around the CVE program is set to push the European effort into the spotlight as a replacement, fallback, or alternative for CVE. ENISA is, we note, a partner of CVE; specifically, it's a CVE numbering authority.
The EUVD "will hopefully gain more traction so that Europe can achieve self-sustainability in this domain as well," Marcus Söderblom, an infosec consultant at IT services giant Atea
said
this week.
Ben Radcliff, senior director of cyber operations at infosec services provider Optiv, told
The Register
Thursday that the CVE funding fiasco revealed a serious flaw: Dependence on the largesse of a single, and now volatile, government.
"Continued dependency on funding from CISA might put pressure on the organization to act and operate with less impartiality and political agnosticism," he added. "One of the key promises of EUVD is that it will be multi-nationally sponsored, ostensibly avoiding that pitfall."
Or, it could present another pitfall: Separate bug tracking systems for the US and Europe. Like imperial versus metric, only worse.
"While it's likely that there will be coordination between the US NVD and the EUVD such that records available in one database mirror those in the other, I do expect that regional regulatory governance will tend to favor one vulnerability database over another," Tim Mackey, head of software supply chain risk strategy at app security firm Black Duck, told
The Register
.
The timing of the EU database's emergence "cannot be ignored as a coincidence," Flashpoint vulnerability analyst Brian Martin said on a Thursday webinar. "To me, it signals a global lack of trust in the US government's commitment to ensuring the continuity of CVE."
Meanwhile, another "global" system for identifying and numbering security flaws, the Global CVE Allocation System or
GCVE
, sprang from CVE's almost-ashes. "But that essentially looks like it's one person on a GitHub project," Martin said.
In addition to these two, there's also the new
CVE Foundation
, a non-profit formed to bring the CVE program under its auspices and eliminate a "single point of failure in the vulnerability management ecosystem."
And, of course, MITRE will continue operating the CVE program per usual under its contract with the Feds — at least for the next 11 months.
"There's no understanding or guarantee about what will happen after that point," Flashpoint vulnerability analyst Kecia Hoyt said on the webinar. "Maybe we can go enjoy our weekend at this point, but I don't want to be here having this conversation a year from now, and nothing's changed."
What's in a name?
Having a standardized system for identifying vulnerabilities is extremely important, and helps keep everyone — companies, vulnerability researchers, developers, governments — on the same page. If someone says
CVE-2017-5754
, for example, there's no question they are talking about Intel's
Meltdown
, which did also show up in a handful of Arm CPU cores.
This common language helps avoid what we currently have with cybercrime-groups, where various government agencies and private-sector threat intel firms all have their own naming conventions — is it
Cozy Bear, Midnight Blizzard, or APT 29
? And how
loosely linked
are Salt Typhoon, Famous Sparrow, and Earth Estries?
"I say
Scattered Spider
, you say
Oktapus
," Hoyt said, referring to two names for the collective of what's suspected to be young US and UK criminals known for their
ransomware heists
of Las Vegas casinos.

data.title: Using –/.ssh/authorized keys to decide what the incoming connection can do
data.author: jandeboevrie
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了通过在 `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` 文件中指定命令来限制 SSH 连接的操作，以实现对 Bacula 数据库和配置备份的安全传输。作者使用 `rrsync` 工具限制 SSH 连接仅能进行指定路径下的只读 `rsync` 操作。为了解决双向备份问题，作者为不同备份任务创建了不同的 SSH 密钥对，并在 `authorized_keys` 文件中配置相应的命令限制。一个密钥对应一个特定操作，确保每个任务独立且安全地运行。这种方法有效保护了重要备份系统的安全性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过SSH在不同主机之间执行受限操作的实现方法及其安全性

不同观点：
• nneonneo认为可以通过在第二主机上创建一个解析和验证文件路径的shell脚本（如"from_host_1"），并通过单个SSH密钥实现多个操作。这种方法简化了在第一主机上通过小脚本进行SSH调用的需求。然而，nneonneo也指出，使用单一SSH密钥在多个主机间共享存在安全风险，如果一台主机被攻陷，风险会增加。因此，他建议在不同主机上使用不同的SSH密钥以降低风险。

• 3np补充了这种方法在Linux主机上结合zfs文件系统和sudoers配置的应用，特别是在需要root权限的远程zfs send/receive操作中非常有用。这强调了在特定场景下，SSH结合权限控制可以实现更复杂的功能。

• pickle-wizard赞同这种方法的实用性，认为它可以很好地限制服务账户的权限。他还指出，SSH有很多不为人知的功能，可以被广泛应用于各种场景中，强调了SSH工具的强大和灵活性。

补充讨论：
• 安全性讨论：nneonneo特别提到了使用单一SSH密钥在多个系统间共享的风险问题，这是实际应用中需要权衡和考虑的重要因素。
• 特定应用场景：3np提到的zfs和root权限操作是一个具体的应用场景，展示了这种方法在实际系统管理中的价值。
• SSH功能的广泛性：pickle-wizard指出SSH的许多功能尚未被广泛了解和使用，暗示这种技术有更多的潜力可以挖掘。

争议焦点：主要争议在于是否应该在多个主机间共享SSH密钥。nneonneo认为共享密钥会增加安全风险，而其他讨论者更关注这种方法的实用性和功能实现。

43724965.article_content:
~/.ssh/authorized_keys
allows you to specify the command run by the incoming ssh connection.
I was searching for a previous blog post to give you some background. I failed.
I backup my Bacula database and my Bacula configuration via rsync. These backups go to more than one host.
The following are lines from
~rsyncer/.ssh/authorized-keys
on my
dbclone
host – which gathers database backups from various hosts.
from="x8dtu.example.org,10.1.1.1",command="/usr/local/sbin/rrsync -ro /usr/home/rsyncer/backups/bacula-database/postgresql/" ssh-ed25519
AAAAC3thisisalsonotmyrealpublickeybcxpFeUMAC2LOitdpRb9l0RoW7vt5hnzwt rsyncer@x8dtu.example.org
The above appears on two lines to make it easier to read without horizontal scrolling – in the file, it’s all on one line.
This says:
* when an ssh connection comes in from a client at
x8dtu.example.org
, or
10.1.1.1
* run
/usr/local/sbin/rrsync -ro /usr/home/rsyncer/backups/bacula-database/postgresql/
* and that client must have this key (as shown)
*
rsyncer@x8dtu.example.org
is a comment, and has no effect
What does
/usr/local/sbin/rrsync -ro /usr/home/rsyncer/backups/bacula-database/postgresql/
do?
See
man rrsync
, a program supplied with rsync. In short it is “script to setup restricted rsync users via ssh logins”.
It means the incoming client can only
rsync
from the specified path
/usr/home/rsyncer/backups/bacula-database/postgresql/
and that the session is
ro
(read-only).
This is a great feature. Given that these passphraseless ssh-keys allow access to a rather important system (it has all the database backups), imposing such restrictions seems a good idea.
This works well for transferring the Bacula database back from
dbclone
over to
x8dtu
.
Now, what if I want to copy a different database backup in the other direction, from
x8dtu
to
dbclone
?
I have previously decided that
dbclone
is a pull-only host. That is nobody can push data to it. My solution: the command specified in ~/.ssh/authorized keys initiates an rsync on
dbclone
, pulling data from
x8dtu
.
That script looks something like this.
[rsyncer@dbclone ~]$ cat /home/rsyncer/bin/rsync-backup-from-x8dtu.sh
#!/bin/sh
#
# This file does a backup of each database on the server.
# It relies upon a file on the server to do the actual backup,
# then uses rsync to copy the files from the server to here.
#
# the ~/.ssh/authorized keys entry on the server must look like this:
#
# from="10.55.0.140",command="/usr/local/sbin/rrsync /usr/home/backups/" [ssh key goes here]
#
# invoking rrsync ensures the incoming rsync process is chrooted to /usr/home/dan/backups/
# Thus, BACKUPDIR is relative to that location.
BACKUPDIR=${HOME}/backups/x8dtu-pg01/database-backup
IDENTITY_FILE_RSYNC=${HOME}/.ssh/id_ed25519
SERVER_TO_RSYNC=x8dtu.example.org
cd ${BACKUPDIR}
#
# use rsync to get local copies
#
/usr/local/bin/rsync -e "/usr/bin/ssh -i ${IDENTITY_FILE_RSYNC}" --recursive -av --stats --progress --exclude 'archive' ${SERVER_TO_RSYNC}:/ ${BACKUPDIR}
Great. Now all I need to do is add another entry into
authorized_keys
on
dbclone
, resulting in something like this:
from="x8dtu.example.org,10.1.1.1",command="/usr/local/sbin/rrsync -ro /usr/home/rsyncer/backups/bacula-database/postgresql/" ssh-ed25519
AAAAC3thisisalsonotmyrealpublickeybcxpFeUMAC2LOitdpRb9l0RoW7vt5hnzwt rsyncer@x8dtu.example.org
from="x8dtu.startpoint.vpn.unixathome.org,10.8.1.100",command="/home/rsyncer/bin/rsync-backup-from-x8dtu.sh" ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3thisisalsonotmyrealpublickeybcxpFeUMAC2LOitdpRb9l0RoW7vt5hnzwt rsyncer@x8dtu.example.org
Here’s the problem. Both lines can’t run.  Only one will run. The incoming ssh key will match, and that command will be run.  Instead. I added a second ssh key:
[rsyncer@x8dtu ~/.ssh]$ ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f id_ed25519.rsync.bacula
...
I modified the above script to use that key:
IDENTITY_FILE_RSYNC=${HOME}/.ssh/id_ed25519.rsync.bacula
Next, I modified
authorized_keys
on
dbclone
to refer to the new public key (again, I’ve added newlines in here so you don’t have to scroll):
from="x8dtu.example.org,10.1.1.1",command="/usr/local/sbin/rrsync -ro /usr/home/rsyncer/backups/bacula-database/postgresql/" ssh-ed25519
AAAAC3thisisalsonotmyrealpublickeybcxpFeUMAC2LOitdpRb9l0RoW7vt5hnzwt rsyncer@x8dtu.example.org
from="x8dtu.startpoint.vpn.unixathome.org,10.8.1.100",command="/home/rsyncer/bin/rsync-backup-from-x8dtu.sh" ssh-ed25519
AAAAC3thisisthesecondsshkeypKBYib6rCHZ+zK5Q3LvJFukdFzT+Q92GUtej6SLW8 rsyncer@x8dtu.example.org
This works.  It means that for each task to be carried out, I need a different ssh key. However, so far, there are just two tasks.
Hope this helps.

data.title: Technicality
data.author: theunamedguy
data.article_summary: "Technicality" 是一个由作者开发的未完成的可缩放字体，灵感来自 Tekton 字体，主要用于 Linux 终端窗口和文本编辑器。它是一种等宽字体，但也包含可变宽度的版本，用于窗口标题。该字体尚未完成，存在字符不全、可变宽度字体侧轴承不规则、缺少 overshoots 和几乎没有提示（hinting）等问题。尽管如此，作者提供了多个格式（OTF、TTF、WOFF）的下载，并公开了 Metafont 源代码。作者的短期目标是改进字体提示和解决字符对齐问题，长期目标则是增加斜体版本。字体目前适合能容忍其缺陷的用户使用。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

43725085.article_content:
Technicality
an unfinished terminal font distantly inspired by Tekton
Introduction
Technicality is my own personal scalable font, which I use in all
my terminal windows and text editors on Linux.
For that purpose, it needs to be a monospaced font. But I also made
a variable-width form of it, which I configure my window manager to
use in window titles.
Itâs rather unfinished, but itâs good enough for
me
to
use. And occasionally people ask me about it, so perhaps it deserves
a web page.
A Linux terminal window in Technicality Mono Bold.
The window title is also in Technicality Bold (variable width).
The image depicts the Emacs editor showing a snippet of the Metafont source code for Technicality itself.
Unfinishedness
Before I offer some download links, I should show you all the
things that are
bad
about this font, in case they make you
decide not to download and use it after all.
Ad-hoc level of completeness
. Iâve added
characters to Technicality on the basis of my own use of it:
whenever I wanted to use a character myself in text, or found other
people using it, and didnât like what my terminal substituted from
some other font, Iâd add it. Anyone else without my exact usage
profile is likely to find missing characters. In fact
even
I
find missing characters.
Weird side bearings in the variable-pitch font
. I
assigned left and right side bearings via an iterative process that
on the one hand
mostly
prevents serious miskerns without
needing too many kerning tables, but on the other hand looks
nonsensical if you view the characters in something like Fontforge â
some perfectly ordinary letters like âbâ overshoot their right side
bearing! This could do with a serious cleanup of
some
kind.
Missing overshoots
. I havenât got round to making
characters with curved bottoms slightly overshoot the baseline.
Thatâs because at the pixel sizes I normally use, it doesnât make a
difference. But at some pixel sizes it looks horrible:
Â Â Â Â
Technicality Mono Bold at two very similar pixel sizes, showing intermittent vertical misalignment.
The left image is aligned sensibly, but the right image has the âbâs too high.
Almost no hinting
. I mostly use Technicality on
Linux, and the Linux font stack seems to be pretty good at managing
without hints. Iâve had mixed success using it on Windows in the
past, which I always thought was probably because Windowsâs
rendering depends more on good hinting. I had a half-finished idea
of trying to automatically code-generate Truetype hint programs from
some simpler description alongside the Metafont code for each
character, which got as far as an initial implementation which
managed to rescue
one
otherwise illegible character
(the
=
sign used to vanish completely at some sizes on
Windows!), but I havenât yet got round to trying to make it work for
everything else too.
In short, Technicality is currently
a
symbiosisware
font: its
only user (at least, up to the point where I published this web
page) has always been its developer, so Iâve only been fixing the
things that seem easier to fix than to put up with.
Downloads
Here are some initial downloads:
technicality-otf.zip
:
OpenType font files. (I prefer these on Linux; install by just
putting the files anywhere under
~/.fonts
.)

43725085.article_summary: "Technicality" 是一个由作者开发的未完成的可缩放字体，灵感来自 Tekton 字体，主要用于 Linux 终端窗口和文本编辑器。它是一种等宽字体，但也包含可变宽度的版本，用于窗口标题。该字体尚未完成，存在字符不全、可变宽度字体侧轴承不规则、缺少 overshoots 和几乎没有提示（hinting）等问题。尽管如此，作者提供了多个格式（OTF、TTF、WOFF）的下载，并公开了 Metafont 源代码。作者的短期目标是改进字体提示和解决字符对齐问题，长期目标则是增加斜体版本。字体目前适合能容忍其缺陷的用户使用。

data.title: Athena – An open source production-ready general AI agent
data.author: yvbbrjdr
data.article_summary: Athena是一个通用的AI代理，旨在将洞察力与执行力结合，帮助用户轻松实现从想法到结果的转化。它具备多种功能，如控制计算机、执行Python代码、自动化网页浏览、搜索、翻译文档、数据可视化、网页抓取等。Athena支持插件扩展，包括命令行控制、文件访问、时间感知与调度、与其他语言模型聊天等。用户可以通过克隆其核心代码库并配置API密钥来启动和使用Athena。其文档采用“Vibe Docs”方式，推荐使用AI解释代码功能。Athena的未来路线图包括实现自主代码编写、增强浏览器自动化、改进上下文管理、支持长期记忆和多模态模型等，目标是实现人类水平的人工智能（AGI）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在生产环境中应使用何种工具或技术，特别是在OpenAI有竞争限制的情况下。

不同观点：
• [bionhoward]认为，OpenAI有竞争限制，因此在实际生产中使用OpenAI并不合适，他质疑在生产环境中应该使用什么替代方案。
• [lucystoll]回应说，可以使用其他开源的AI模型或工具，例如TensorFlow、PyTorch或Hugging Face等，这些工具没有竞争限制，并且在某些场景下表现良好。
• [mikedev]指出，尽管OpenAI有竞争限制，但仍然可以用于研究和开发阶段，而在生产环境中切换到其他无竞争限制的平台，如自研模型或者第三方无限制的API。

补充讨论：
• [lucystoll]提到，OpenAI的限制主要针对直接竞争产品，因此在某些非竞争性的商业场景下，可能仍然可以使用OpenAI的服务，但需要仔细审查其使用条款。
• [mikedev]建议，开发者应关注AI领域的新兴技术和工具，以便在面对限制时有更多的选择和灵活性。
• [bionhoward]进一步质疑，如何在保证性能和效果的前提下，找到合适的替代方案，这可能是很多开发者共同面临的挑战。

争议焦点：OpenAI的竞争限制对生产环境中AI工具选择的影响，以及如何找到合适的替代方案以满足性能和合规要求。

data.title: The "De" in "Decentralization" Stands for "Democracy"
data.author: nickcotter
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Fediverse（联邦宇宙）的去中心化特性及其优势。作者指出，Fediverse的“秘密武器”在于网络本身的重要性，而非个别网站。即使某个实例（instance）下线，用户可以轻松迁移到其他实例，而不会与好友失联。这种设计与传统网站不同，以前网站下线是常态，而现在的大型平台因拥有强大的技术支持很少出现这种情况。Fediverse允许用户在实例遭受法律问题或技术故障时，迁移到其他国家的实例，避免单点故障。相比之下，如果类似Bluesky这样的平台被不良势力收购，用户将无处可去。即使Mastodon创始人退出，整个网络仍能正常运作。这种去中心化结构提供了更大的弹性和自由。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对“DTA”这一缩写的不同解释

不同观点：
• 观点一：[dtagames] 认为“DTA”常代表“delusion”（妄想）或 “defraud”（欺骗）。这一解释带有负面含义，暗示使用该缩写的人可能涉及某种误导或欺骗行为。

补充讨论：
• 该评论没有提供具体的背景或例子来支持其观点，但通过选择“delusion”和“defraud”这两个词，可以看出评论者对“DTA”缩写持负面评价。
• 没有其他观点或反驳意见出现在该评论中，因此尚无明显争议或对话关系。

43725755.article_content:
I’m reminded of
something I read on the Fediverse yesterday
; I’ll quote it at length with no changes in formatting:
the secret sauce of the fediverse is that the network is the important part. the websites die but the network keeps going. even if your instance dies in a blaze of glory or whatever, you go somewhere else and your friends are still there.
you see nerds on other websites not understand this. they’re like “fedi instances go down all the time”. yeah, but individual instances don’t matter. your friends are still there. you just go to a different instance. you didn’t have to convince your friends to follow you on a different website because they keep going to the same one.
also, you gotta remember, websites went down all the time before now. that was just a fact of life before the modern age of the googles and the facebooks and such with giant data centers and 24/7 on call engineers. like it used to be websites would go down for a while and you’d say “well, i guess i’ll go somewhere else until Greg wakes up and fixes it”
we’re used to it by now. usually you get some warning when an instance is gonna go down permanently so you get a chance to ask your friends if they have room on their instance. it’s annoying, but, again, it’s less traumatic than having to leave, say, twitter, because you don’t have to convince your friends to move
instances die, the network lives on. as it should be.
meanwhile, if bluesky gets bought by hitler 2, you’re shit out of luck
you ever think about how eugen could quit this and pull the plug on mastodon.social tomorrow and we’d be basically fine
… also, like, if your instance gets a nastygram from a government, or if you can’t pay for your domain because of sanctions against the taliban, you can move to an instance in a different country. that’s pretty nice.

data.title: Waiting 100 years for a home isn't a housing crisis, it's a moral collapse
data.author: microflash
data.article_summary: 作者Kunle Barker讲述了自己对社会住房理解的转变。他从一个建筑环境从业者的角度，认识到良好的住房不仅提供庇护，还能改变生活。通过一次将两居室改造成四居室的项目，他亲眼看到一个女孩因拥有自己房间而能够专心学习，立志成为医生。这让他意识到小到学习空间的 privilege 对人生发展的重要性。然而，英国目前面临严重的社会住房危机，部分地区的家庭需要等待超过100年才能获得合适的住房。尽管政府承诺建设150万套住房，但社会住房问题依然严峻，市场无法解决这一问题。作者呼吁进行立法改革、激励措施、以及全行业的技能提升，以应对这场危机。他认为必须集思广益，采取多种解决方案，不能再拖延。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国住房危机的成因及解决办法

不同观点：
• **nly的观点**：过去50-70年里，英国选择停止建设社会住房并出售现有住房，同时提供政府补贴。如今对住房问题的抱怨是无用的，因为问题早在20-30年前就该提出。购房者依赖不断上涨的房价，如果房价回归可负担水平，已有房产者将受到影响。英国的住房问题已持续几十年，无论是房主还是租房者都面临困境。

• **bwb的观点**：评判政府有效性的一个重要标准是住房成本。经济实惠的住房对经济福祉至关重要。建议政府大规模建设小型公寓以满足需求，特别是在经济中心地区。同时，提问还有什么其他标准可以用来评估政府的有效性。

• **whatever1的观点**：远程工作的机会未能缓解住房危机，因为机会集中在少数大城市，而这些地区的住房建设速度难以满足需求。大城市的规模化和运营问题尚未解决，因此住房危机不会很快消失。

• **untoasted12的观点**：质疑是否有评论者实际阅读了文章，因为链接已失效。

• **brap的观点**：住房危机的核心问题是建设速度不足，但未深入探讨原因。

• **globular-toast的观点**：可能是链接访问量过大导致页面失效（“拥抱死亡”现象）。

• **milesrout的观点**：不需要等待100年才能获得住房，可以立即购买或租房，但未提及住房可负担性问题。

• **somewhereoutth的观点**：英国缺乏中等高度的公寓楼，多为低密度的排屋，导致住房密度不足。相比之下，葡萄牙的中高层公寓建筑提供了更高的居住密度和良好的生活条件。

• **coolThingsFirst的观点**：简单表达了对住房的需求。

43726261.article_content:
I didn’t grow up in social housing. My childhood was spent in an architecturally unremarkable housing development in a picture-postcard Bedfordshire village. My understanding of council homes was, if I’m honest, limited and filtered through stereotypes. It wasn’t until I started working in the built environment that I began to grasp what social housing really meant: not just shelter but something that could fundamentally change lives.
One early project with
CityWest Homes
underlined that. We converted a two-bed flat into a four-bedroom duplex in a prime London postcode. It was, at the time, the biggest and most complex job we’d taken on. When the work was done, I walked the site with the client, proud of the team’s achievement. A young girl living there thanked me. I nodded politely, but she stopped me. ‘No, you don’t understand,’ she said. ‘I finally have my own room. I used to share with my brothers. Now I can do my homework. I want to be a doctor, and now I have somewhere to study.’
That moment reframed everything. Small privileges we take for granted, like a space to think, are often the foundations for ambition. A good home can unlock someone’s potential. So, the recent news that families in parts of England face waits of over 100 years for suitably sized social homes shines a harsh light on what the housing crisis actually means.
Advertisement
Research from the National Housing Federation
, Shelter, and Crisis found that in 32 council areas, the wait is longer than 18 years. In some London boroughs, it’s over a century. More than 1.3 million families are on waiting lists. A record 164,000 children live in temporary accommodation. These aren’t numbers; they’re lives paused.
This isn’t just a crisis; it’s a moral collapse. And it’s not even surprising. In my ‘
Ghost of Housing’ column
, I warned that the unthinkable was becoming inevitable thanks to the consequences of decades of inertia.
We need to abandon the fantasy that the market will fix this
Even with the government’s pledge to build 1.5 million homes during this Parliament, the elephant in the room is social housing. It’s expensive, risky, and currently unviable. Developers are lining up to build luxury flats, but ask for decent homes for working families, and you’ll hear silence.
Why? Because the numbers don’t stack up. We lack skilled labour. We lack incentives. And we’re operating under a planning system that actively works against what we need.
The government may be saying the right things, but it needs to show the courage to act. That means radical legislative reform: easy-build zones, streamlined permissions, tax incentives, and rethinking ownership models. And we must upskill the entire industry to ensure we have the right people working in the right areas.
Advertisement
We also need to abandon the fantasy that the market will fix this. Help to Buy and shared ownership are sticking plasters. Social housing isn’t a safety net; it’s the foundation of a fair society.
A century-long wait is a national disgrace. We can’t keep recycling the same discussions while the crisis deepens. Those of us in the industry must speak plainly and act collectively.
I hear many views on what needs to change: housing density, green or grey belt use, rural or edge-of-city growth, land valuations, planning reform. And they’re all valid. We need all of these solutions.
That’s what the 100-year waiting list reminded me about. We can’t wait for a single, unified masterplan to emerge, because time isn’t on our side. Instead, we need to back every serious idea that could meaningfully shift the dial. That means supporting colleagues who advocate for densification and infill as much as those calling for land release on the green or grey belt. It means listening to planners and architects, local authorities and housing associations. Each can add a piece of the puzzle.
Above all, it means speaking clearly and with urgency. If you’re working in this space, your voice matters. If you have a solution, however local or specific, it’s worth hearing. The problem we face is too big for silence or for silos. So speak up, speak out, and support each other. We are running out of time.
Kunle Barker is a property expert, journalist and broadcaster

data.title: Less Slow C++
data.author: ashvardanian
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了`less_slow.cpp`项目，旨在帮助开发者学习如何编写高效的C和C++代码，涵盖从基础数值计算到高级并发、异常处理和网络编程等内容。项目提供了多种性能优化的实例，包括利用C++20特性、SIMD、协程、范围（ranges）、矩阵乘法优化、CUDA、PTX和汇编等技术。文章强调了现代代码中常见的性能问题，如输入生成成本、三角函数计算、分支预测、多线程扩展等，并提供了多种优化技巧，如使用`std::error_code`、`consteval`正则表达式、`io_uring`处理网络请求等。此外，项目还比较了不同编译器、库（如OpenMP、oneTBB）和硬件架构（CPU、GPU、FPGA）的性能差异，适合在Linux环境下使用GCC和Clang编译器进行实践。项目代码和基准测试可在多平台运行，推荐通过CMake进行构建。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同技术话题的讨论，包括代码优化、嵌入式系统开发、库的选择与使用、以及对高性能计算的关注。

不同观点：
• [kllrnohj] 对通过减少计算项来加速三角函数（如std::sin）的方法提出批评，认为这种优化虽然在计算速度上有所提升，但精度损失严重，特别是在输入值超出[-2, 2]范围时，结果非常不准确。
• [boricj] 分享了在嵌入式系统开发中的经验，强调在资源受限的环境下，不同的优化策略是必要的。例如，避免使用可能导致栈溢出的正则表达式库（CTRE），以及为了减少内存分配和碎片化而自行编写BSON库。此外，还提到为了节省程序空间而替换C/C++标准库的某些部分。
• [vitus] 对使用Abseil库的关联容器提出质疑，认为虽然Abseil曾经是一个不错的选择，但现在有其他替代品（如Boost的unordered_flat_map）可能更优，并指出Abseil在一些设计选择上存在问题。

补充讨论：
• [loeg] 认为整个讨论内容杂乱无章，缺乏连贯性，不适合作为深入学习的资源。
• [EliRivers] 对FPGA与GPU编码以及高层次综合（HLS）、Verilog和VHDL的区别表示兴趣，提出希望了解相关内容。
• [kreetx] 对内容的简洁和实用性表示赞赏。
• [spieswl] 对之前发布的Google Benchmark文章表示赞赏，并表示对性能基准测试的关注。
• [standy13] 对非规范化浮点数表示好奇，并提到在GPU矩阵运算中的应用。
• [nickysielicki] 推荐了Kris Jusiak的GitHub项目作为其他有价值的资源。
• [johnisgood] 指出文章中提到的一些C++代码使用了大量的C++特性，而没有真正的C代码，建议修改标题或内容以避免误导。
• [intelVISA] 询问C++在io_uring上的异步（协程）支持情况。
• [hwpythonner] 认为这些内容可以打包成高性能计算的手册或实用指南，特别是对高频交易（HFT）开发者有帮助。
• [Icathian] 希望找到Rust语言的类似资源，询问推荐的书籍或项目。
• [jonstewart] 对C++中以“性能”为名进行的复杂优化表示怀疑，认为需要更多的实证数据支持，但对CTRE库的性能表示意外，并计划进一步研究。

争议焦点：
• 三角函数优化方法的实用性，特别是在精度和速度之间的权衡。
• Abseil库的优劣以及是否应选择其他替代品。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 嵌入式系统中的优化策略，包括避免栈溢出和减少内存分配的具体方法。
• 对高性能计算和特定技术（如FPGA、HLS）的兴趣和需求。
• 对C++和其他编程语言（如Rust）资源和优化方法的需求和推荐。

data.title: A New ASN.1 API for Python
data.author: woodruffw
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了ASN.1在加密学、网络协议和Python中的重要性及其面临的挑战，并宣布了一个新的ASN.1 API开发计划。ASN.1是一种数据结构描述语法，广泛应用于TLS握手、X.509证书验证、LDAP、SNMP等核心网络协议中。然而，其历史上有许多内存损坏和拒绝服务漏洞。当前Python中的ASN.1库（如pyasn1）性能不足，且容易导致解析差异风险。

为了解决这些问题，一个新的ASN.1 API将集成到PyCA Cryptography中，具备以下特点：
1. **性能**：使用Rust编写，提升解析速度。
2. **减少差异**：与现有X.509 API共享解析器，降低差异风险。
3. **现代化**：采用声明式dataclasses风格接口，支持类型提示。

该项目由Alpha-Omega资助，延续了此前Sovereign Tech Fund支持的X.509路径验证工作，旨在改善Python在加密学和供应链安全方面的生态系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ASN.1及其不同编码规则（尤其是DER和UPER）的应用、性能、工具支持及社区讨论。

不同观点：
• **历史背景与DER的选择**：ChuckMcM回顾了历史，指出在早期选择ASN.1 DER编码是因为需要与OSI兼容，并且认为在"握手"阶段，确定性比性能更重要。

• **ASN.1的实用性**：orthecreedence分享了自己从msgpack转向ASN.1 DER的经历，认为ASN.1 DER对于需要签名和序列化的系统非常有用，避免了自己定义序列化格式。

• **Rust库的性能优势**：nicce提到rasn库在Rust中对多种ASN.1编码规则的支持，并声称OER编码在开源世界中性能最优，甚至超过了Google的Protobuf库。

• **ASN.1的学习价值**：flowerthoughts建议在创建自定义序列化格式时应了解ASN.1，因其在描述和编码规则上非常完整。

• **历史使用经验**：time4tea分享了20多年前使用ASN.1进行微服务通信的经验，认为其性能良好，但需要购买OSS工具许可证。

• **Erlang和Java的支持问题**：johnisgood提到Erlang对ASN.1的支持很好，但对OSS Nokalva的专有解决方案不满，并询问其他Java工具的推荐。

• **UPER的难度和工具缺乏**：dikei指出UPER编码规则在电信行业很普遍，但缺乏免费可用工具。

• **对OSS Nokalva的批评**：venamresm__希望OSS Nokalva的专有解决方案能被替代。

• **Wireshark集成的可能性**：woodrowbarlow提到ASN.1文件可用于创建Wireshark解析器。

• **安全问题**：mootptr强调了ASN.1解析器的安全问题，特别是差分利用攻击。

• **asn1 crate的限制**：lilyball指出asn1 crate在处理CHOICE类型时的限制，无法用于实现X.509证书解码。

• **Python社区的讨论**：benatkin和dec0dedab0de讨论了Python社区中对"纯Python"实现与性能优化之间的权衡，以及对混合使用编译二进制和Python回退的期望。

补充讨论：
• ASN.1工具的现状和未来发展：讨论中涉及了多种语言对ASN.1的支持情况，以及对开源工具性能和易用性的期望。
• 专有解决方案与开源替代：对OSS Nokalva专有解决方案的不满和对开源替代的期待。
• 不同编码规则的适用场景：如DER和UPER在不同行业中的应用及其工具支持的差异。

If you’ve ever worked with cryptography, PKI schemes, or low-level networking
in Python, you’ve likely encountered
ASN.1
.
ASN.1 undergirds every TLS handshake (via
X.509
path validation),
provides the serialization layer for core internet protocols like
LDAP
,
SNMP
,
and
3GPP
, and generally operates as the
lingua franca
of cryptographic
primitive and protocol representation.
ASN.1’s critical role is complemented by a colorful security history:
implementations of ASN.1’s encoding rules have historically been a
rich source of
memory corruption and denial-of-service vulnerabilities
. Similarly,
ASN.1’s presence at the lowest layers of the internet’s protocols
makes performance and a lack of
parser differentials
a critical requirement.
Python has multiple excellent ASN.1 implementations (like
pyasn1
,
asn1
, and
asn1tools
), but these generally
fall into the latter category: being written purely in Python makes performance
a concern, and integration into a stack where other ASN.1 parsers are used
(e.g., at the X.509 layer) introduces a differential risk.
We’re changing that: with the help of funding from
Alpha-Omega
,
we’re building an ASN.1 API for
PyCA Cryptography
that addresses
three key shortcomings in the Python ecosystem today:
Performance
: This new API will use a
pure Rust ASN.1 parser
,
giving us close-to-native parsing performance.
Differential reduction
: The parser mentioned above is already used
by
PyCA Cryptography
for its X.509 APIs. This will reduce the need for
“mix and match” approaches to ASN.1 parsing, which in turn drive
differential vulnerabilities.
Modernization
: The new API will expose a declarative
dataclasses
style interface replete with type hints, making it familiar, idiomatic,
and compatible with type checkers.
For example, an ASN.1 definition like this:
Doohickies ::= SEQUENCE {
tschotchkes       OCTET STRING,
baubles           INTEGER,
knickknacks       UTF8String,
whatchamacallits  SEQUENCE OF OBJECT IDENTIFIER,
gizmos            SET OF GeneralizedTime OPTIONAL
}
…will correspond to the following Python code:
from
datetime
import
datetime
from
cryptography.hazmat
import
asn1
@asn1.sequence
class
Doohickies
:
tschotchkes
:
bytes
baubles
:
int
knickknacks
:
str
whatchamacallits
:
list
[
asn1
.
ObjectIdentifier
]
gizmos
:
set
[
datetime
]
|
None
doohickies
=
Doohickies
.
from_der
(
b
"..."
)
print
(
doohickies
.
tschotchkes
)
doohickies
.
to_der
()
# b"..."
This work is a logical continuation of our previous work on
X.509 path validation
, as funded by the
Sovereign Tech Fund
. It
reflects our ongoing commitment to improving the Python ecosystem, particularly
in the areas of cryptography and supply chain security.
Please
get in touch
if you’re interested in learning more, or funding
similar work!
Some quick background on ASN.1
ASN.1
, or Abstract Syntax Notation One, is an
interface description language
(IDL). That’s a fancy way of saying that it’s a syntax for describing
data structures in a language- and platform-agnostic manner.
Confusingly, ASN.1 is
not itself
a serialization format. Instead, it defines
encoding rules
, which in turn define serialization and deserialization
of ASN.1 structures in different settings. In practice,
ASN.1 is synonymous
1
with the
Distinguished Encoding Rules
, or DER.
Figure 1: A helpful visual explanation of ASN.1's different encoding rules
We’ll treat “ASN.1” and “DER” as interchangeable for the purposes of this post.
Instead of delving too deeply into the intricacies of both
(
Let’s Encrypt covers them excellently
), we’ll focus on the properties
of DER that have kept it relevant for decades:
DER is a
canonical
encoding:
There’s only one way to encode a given ASN.1
structure in DER. In other words, the encoding of an ASN.1 structure in DER
is deterministic and can be round-tripped while preserving bit-for-bit
equality.
DER is
relatively compact
:
DER defines a binary format and, as a
consequence of being canonical, forbids non-minimal encodings of integers,
booleans, and times.
DER is a
self-describing
and
self-delimiting
encoding:
A given DER
message can be fully and soundly parsed without prior reference to a
schema or format description beyond the encoding rules of DER themselves.
These properties lend themselves naturally to what web developers would
call “progressive enhancement”: an application that consumes DER can
decode the specific structures it cares about while skipping the ones it
doesn’t, decoding only their length in order to jump ahead to the next one.
DER supports
arbitrary-precision integers
:
The
INTEGER
type in DER
is functionally unconstrained in size, which makes it suitable for
representing the kinds of large numbers that regularly appear in
cryptographic settings (e.g., primes).
Put together, these properties make DER very popular in cryptographic,
networking, and telecommunications settings.

data.title: Walled Gardens Can Kill
data.author: steelbrain
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了一位长期使用苹果生态系统的用户在紧急情况下遇到的困境。作者的妻子突然生病，需要确定可去的医院，但由于其保险公司的应用程序地理限制，无法在iPhone上安装。更麻烦的是，更改苹果账户地区需要先取消Apple Music订阅，时间紧迫无法完成。最终，作者利用之前因开发安卓应用而在笔记本上安装的安卓模拟器解决了问题。这次经历让作者改变了对苹果封闭生态的看法，认为像DMA这样的法律应全球推行，以避免类似困境。作者现在备有一部安卓手机以应对紧急情况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple设备上的区域锁定应用以及技术依赖带来的问题

不同观点：
• **photonthug**：认为问题不仅限于Apple，而是所有应用程序都可能因技术故障或用户过度依赖而导致危险情况。提到现代人过度依赖手机地图导致迷路等风险，并指出技术公司有责任考虑这些极端情况，否则可能因疏忽导致人员伤亡。
  
• **itsanaccount**：批评大公司限制自由，并质疑软件文化是否正在让世界变得更糟。认为企业和政府都存在问题，但对企业通过限制用户自由来增加参与度的做法持批评态度。

• **bee_rider**：将责任归咎于保险公司，指出紧急情况下要求用户选择合适的医院是不合理的。认为Apple不应该为社会功能失调负责，核心问题在于保险系统的设计不合理。

• **dahart**：认为将区域锁定应用的问题全归咎于Apple不公平，指出这是应用开发者的选择，且Android系统也存在类似问题。质疑是否Android能更好地解决此类问题。

• **smallerfish**：分享了在使用Apple TV服务时遇到的技术问题，包括支付和区域限制，反映了Apple生态系统在用户体验上的一些不便。

• **netsharc**：提到在外国的经历，因区域锁定问题无法安装当地ISP的应用，质疑是否应为短期需求更改账户区域设置。

• **Liftyee**：对Apple产品在设计和用户体验上的优势表示赞赏，但对其硬件和软件的锁定政策持批评态度。个人妥协是未来有钱时仍会购买Apple产品。

• **mrangle**：认为文章的前提是错误的，用户可以通过浏览器访问保险公司的网站获取信息，而不是依赖应用。批评文章是博取点击和制造争议。

• **rcMgD2BwE72F**：质疑为何需要应用来获取保险信息，认为保险公司应提供移动网站。

• **steelbrain**：因最近的事件转而支持侧载（sideloading）软件，认为这是绕过封闭生态系统的有效方式。

• **jmull**：认为用户应能自由安装软件，但指出此案例的核心问题不仅是技术限制，还有信息获取的渠道问题。认为依赖应用获取紧急医疗信息是不合理的。

• **touwer**：质疑保险公司为何不提供移动网站，认为依赖应用是不合理的。

• **jimkleiber**：希望未来互联网和人类能够超越地域限制，实现全球化，并对当前基于地域的管理制度表示怀疑。

• **dariosalvi78**：认为不应依赖应用处理生命关键事务，电话等传统方式更可靠。

• **amiantos**：认为文章将责任全推给Apple是不公平的，指出区域锁定是保险公司的决定，Apple仅提供技术支持。并指出Android也有类似问题，批评针对单一公司的抨击是无知或偏见。

补充讨论：
- 技术依赖和应用限制带来的潜在风险，特别是在紧急情况下。
- 企业和政府在技术限制和用户自由之间的平衡问题。
- 不同用户对Apple封闭生态系统的复杂态度，既赞赏其设计和用户体验，又对其限制政策感到不满。
- 对技术公司责任的讨论，特别是在影响广泛用户群体时的安全和责任问题。
- 对区域锁定和技术壁垒的普遍不满，以及可能的解决方案（如侧载、VPN）。

43726672.article_content:
I'm an Apple ecosystem user, owning an iPhone ever since a past employer got it for me to test our company app some 8 years ago. Over time, as I've upgraded, I've also incrementally moved over my family to the ecosystem, replacing our hp/dell laptops with macbooks and Samsung Galaxy phones with Apple iPhones.
Apple's application ecosystem is pretty famously locked down. You cannot side load applications onto your iPhone, quite as easily as you can with an Android. There has been some legislative push to change this (with the EU enacting the Digital Markets Acts or DMA) but the sentiments among lawmakers and users are still divided.
I didn't feel strongly about this, one way or the other until the experiences of last week. My wife suddenly fell ill and we had to figure out which hospital to go to, we were ill-prepared for this situation as we hadn't installed the insurance providers' application to check the in-network hospitals.
Unfortunately for us, the insurance app is geo-restricted to United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Apple refused to install it on my phone. Normally this would be a simply problem to fix, just go to your Apple account settings and switch the region, but this too was denied, as I had the yearly Apple Music subscription. Changing the region in this case required calling Apple Support to cancel the yearly Apple Music subscription first, and we didn't have the time for this.
Luckily I was prototyping with the idea of an Android Application the past week so I had the Android Emulator in my laptop, which I used to install the application, add our insurance information and figure out where to go. Just to be safe, I also ordered an Android phone to be delivered to me while I went to the hospital, where I used my iPhone's hotspot to set it up and show all the insurance information to the hospital staff.
Had I not prototyped the Android Application the week prior, or had Android similarly locked down their ecosystem, we would've been in a much worse situation. This experience has significantly changed my opinions on the matter, I now carry a spare Android phone at home with all the insurance information loaded
just in case
.
Walled Gardens can kill. I hope Apple, the lawmakers and users will reconsider their stance and consider a worldwide DMA-like law to prevent others from falling down the same path.

data.author: susam
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了海洋潮汐对地球自转的影响，分为两种效应。一种是长期效应，由潮汐摩擦导致地球自转逐渐变慢，每世纪一天长度增加约2.3毫秒，这是插入闰秒的原因之一。这种减速主要是由于海洋摩擦引起的，尽管具体机制尚未完全确定。另一种是快速变化效应，由潮汐运动引发地球自转的微小但迅速的改变，变化周期与潮汐周期一致，如半日潮、日潮等。这种快速变化通过两种机制实现：潮水移动改变地球的惯性矩，以及潮汐流与固体地球交换角动量。要预测这些变化，需要全球潮汐高度和潮汐流的模型。此外，长期潮汐也会影响自转和极移。文章还提到了一些经典但部分过时的相关书籍。

不同观点：

• morninglight 没有直接回应计算是否错误，而是提供了一个关于潮汐计算的参考资料（Charles Petzold 的 "Computer of the Tides" 视频），引导对数学和计算机模拟潮汐变化有兴趣的人去查看更多背景资料。这表明他认为通过进一步学习相关知识可以更好地理解这个问题。

补充讨论：
• PopAlongKid 的评论暗示了一个具体的计算问题，即将每世纪 2.3 毫秒的日长增加速率转换到 1000 天后的时间差，可能存在理解或计算上的困惑。他并没有直接否定科学数据，而是对具体的数学换算有疑问。
• morninglight 的回应则是间接的，通过引导观看视频来帮助理解地球自转与潮汐之间的关系，暗示复杂的天文和物理计算需要更多的背景知识，而不是简单的即时计算。
