43697252.article_content:
Ocean Tides and the Earth's Rotation
An Introductory Discussion Courtesy of the
IERS Special Bureau for Tides
Tides affect the earth's rotation in two sharply contrasting ways.
One way, caused by tidal friction, produces an extremely slow secular
change in rotation.  The other way, caused by the continual movements
of the tides about the planet, produces very small but
very rapid changes in rotation.  These rapid changes occur at exactly
the same periods as the tides themselves -- half-daily, daily, etc.
(The IERS
Special Bureau for Tides
is concerned
primarily with the rapid changes,
but some of our data have implications for the secular changes.)
Secular Tidal Braking of Earth Rotation
The secular change in the planet's rotation is a classical topic in
geophysics.  It goes back some 300 years to when
Sir Edmond Halley
first
hypothesized that the moon was accelerating in its orbit.
Most of Halley's lunar acceleration was only apparent.
It was actually the earth's rotation slowing down, making the
moon appear to accelerate.
The moon does accelerate (strictly, it decelerates), but the larger
effect is the earth's rotational braking.
This braking is caused by tidal friction.
Throughout the earth's history tidal braking
has played, and it will continue to play, a dominant role in the rotation.
Currently the secular change in the rotation rate increases the length
of day by some 2.3 milliseconds per day per century.
To see what that means, consider this example: suppose the rotating earth
is our clock and it's been 100 years since that clock's "standard second"
was set to correspond to an atomic clock's second (which is actually almost
the case, notwithstanding that atomic clocks weren't around until 1955).
Then after 1000 days our earth clock loses about 2.3 seconds,
falling further behind the atomic clock.
This long-term slowing of the rotation is a primary reason
for periodically inserting leap seconds into
our timekeeping.  Of course, there are other contributors to the
changing rotation rate such as the changing atmosphere and the
motions of the fluid core; one can't blame just tides for our
timekeeping difficulties.
The tidal braking in the earth's rotation is actually
caused primarily by friction in the oceans,
where ``friction'' may refer to any number of physical mechanisms
which have yet to be determined definitively.  For example, bottom
friction, induced by tidal currents flowing across the seabed, various kinds of
wave breaking, and scattering of tidal waves into oceanic internal waves
are all thought to play a role.  For a recent overview of this subject, look up
Walter Munk
's paper ``Once again: once again--tidal friction,''
published in
Progress in Oceanography,
vol. 40, pp. 7-36, 1997.
Rapid Tidal Variations in Earth Rotation
Only in the last few years has this subject come to the fore,
as our abilities to measure daily and even subdaily variations in
rotation have been developed and improved.
An example is shown on the following figure, which displays very rapid
variations in the rotation rate (in terms of Universal Time) as
observed by hourly measurements and as predicted by a numerical model
of ocean tides.  The measurements are from an intensive campaign of
Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI)
observations, analyzed and
provided courtesy of Chopo Ma and John Gipson (NASA/GSFC).
The ocean predictions are from one of the models provided in the
Special Bureau for Tides
web pages.
Rapid variations in Universal Time as measured by VLBI and
as predicted by a numerical ocean model.
As can be seen, both diurnal and semidiurnal variations are present
in UT1, and they appear to be quite well represented by the ocean model.
There are two ways that the ocean tides can cause such rapid variations.
(1) As the tides move water around the globe,
the moment of inertia of the earth changes.  By conservation of angular
momentum, the solid earth changes its rotation rate accordingly.
(2) As the tidal currents slow down or speed up, they exchange angular
momentum with the solid earth, which is manifested in the rotation rate.
Mechanism (2) is slightly more important for rotation rate variations;
both mechanisms are about equally important for polar motion variations.
Hence, to predict tidal variations in earth rotation, similar to the
solid curve in the figure, requires a global model of both tidal heights and
tidal currents.  The relevant information from several such models is provided
in these web pages of the
Special Bureau for Tides
.
Finally,
there are also tidal variations in rotation rate and polar motion caused
by the near-equilibrium long-period tides, which have periods from about
9 days to 18.6 years.  For rotation rate, the dominant contributor is
in fact the solid-earth tides.  But perturbations from the ocean are
still significant.

additional information
.

data.title: A Math Lesson From Hitler’s Germany (2017)
data.author: perihelions
data.article_summary: 文章回顾了1934年德国数学家大卫·希尔伯特与纳粹教育部长的一段对话，揭示纳粹政策对哥廷根大学数学研究的毁灭性影响，导致大量顶尖数学家被迫离开，美国因此取而代之成为数学研究的中心。文章警示当前美国在特朗普政府下可能面临类似的科学危机，特别是对专家和事实证据的漠视，可能对环境和气候科学造成严重影响。学者担心“后真相”时代的到来，即真相不再重要，符合信念的故事成为主流，这与纳粹时期对科学理性的打压有相似之处。文章呼吁重视历史教训，保护科学研究的独立性和客观性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：二战期间及战后科学家遭遇的政治迫害与学术自由的丧失，以及其对当代学术界和社会的启示。

不同观点：
• **对德国学术界与纳粹勾结的历史揭示**：tlogan指出，许多德国大学的教授在纳粹崛起时积极支持该政权，参与了对犹太学者和持不同政见者的清洗。这不仅是历史注脚，也是对知识机构可能犯错的警示。引用的书籍和文章详细探讨了这一现象。
  
• **对被迫害科学家的个例关注**：ccorcos提到数学家Emmy Noether的经历，她因犹太身份在1933年被迫离开 Göttingen大学，突显了纳粹政权对学术界的破坏。

• **对学术自由受政治压制的反思**：hackandthink引用Saunders Mac Lane的观点，指出政治压力对学术和数学研究的损害，强调了学术独立的重要性。

• **对现代社会信任危机的讨论**：nonrandomstring将历史事件与当代的认知危机联系起来，讨论了在数字化时代对真相和事实的信任危机，并提到这种危机如何被利用来获取控制。

• **不同政治背景下的移民观点对比**：hintymad提到中国移民在美国对政治党派的不同看法，一些移民因过去的创伤经历而对民主党持怀疑态度，而另一些则对共和党的威权倾向保持警惕。

• **对纳粹时期个人反抗的纪念**：thadt引用了Hans Scholl的言论和遭遇，强调了在极权 regime下知识分子反抗的勇气和牺牲。

• **对历史事件后续影响的讨论**：achenet提到Hilbert对 Göttingen数学研究所因犹太人离开而遭受损失的回应，突显了纳粹政策对学术机构的毁灭性影响。

• **对Operation Paperclip的提及**：dirtyhippiefree指出二战后美国对德国科学家的招募行动，揭示了历史事件的复杂后续影响。

• **对未来政治局势的担忧**：holtkam2对特朗普连任的可能性表示担忧，并质疑为何大多数人假设其任期仅为四年，提出了对权力交接的疑虑。

• **对当代学术腐败的批评**：photochemsyn将历史事件与当代美国学术腐败联系起来，指出自1980年代以来大学研究的商业化导致的欺诈和不信任问题。

• **对当前学术界移民潮的担忧**：iterance提到其学术同行中有人考虑移民，反映了当前学术界职业前景的不确定性和对未来的忧虑。

补充讨论：
• **历史与当代的对比与警示**：许多评论将历史事件与当代社会和学术界的问题进行对比，警示当前学术自由和独立性可能面临的威胁。

• **个人经历与历史事件的交织**：评论中既有对历史事件的分析，也有个人和当代学术界人士的经历和反思，提供了多角度的讨论。

I
n 1934, David Hilbert
, by then a grand old man of German mathematics, was dining with Bernhard Rust, the Nazi minister of education. Rust asked, “How is mathematics at Göttingen, now that it is free from the Jewish influence?” Hilbert replied, “There is no mathematics in Göttingen anymore.”
“There is no mathematics in Göttingen anymore”: the German math giant David Hilbert.
Visual: Shelby White and Leon Levy Archives Center, Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, NJ, USA.
Or so the story goes. It is folklore at this point, a story mathematicians tell one another over coffee while exchanging knowing looks. The details vary in different retellings, but every version has Hilbert speaking this truth to power: Nazis destroyed mathematics at the University of Göttingen. “It’s one of the most well-known stories in the history of science,” says Reinhard Siegmund-Schultze, a math historian at the University of Agder in Norway. “Göttingen was so dominant in mathematics internationally.”
In 1933, that dominance came crashing down
. On April 7, two months after Hitler became chancellor, Germany
passed a law
making it illegal for Jews — or rather those considered Jewish by the Nazis — and Communists to hold civil service jobs, with a few exceptions including for people who had served Germany in World War I. That immediately forced several Göttingen mathematicians from their jobs. The crisis snowballed, and over the course of the year, a total of 18 left or were driven out.
By the time of Hilbert’s legendary dinner with Rust, Germany had lost its status as the world’s foremost country for mathematical research. America took its place — and today, though globalization has spread the wealth, the U.S. has retained its eminence. From
Princeton
and
Columbia
to
Berkeley
and
Stanford
, it’s hard to find a great math department in the United States that was not
shaped in part by European mathematicians
who came to or stayed in the U.S. because of the Nazis.
As a new administration with a pronounced anti-science bent takes power in the United States, some scholars are recalling what happened at Göttingen as a cautionary tale. Donald Trump is not Hitler, of course, and “history doesn’t repeat,” as Siegmund-Schultze puts it. Still, he quickly adds, “One also knows from pain that mankind doesn’t really learn from history. Otherwise we wouldn’t do all the same foolish things all the time.”
American democracy is far stronger and longer-lived than was Germany’s between the wars. But we should take the similarities seriously. “I think what you see in both cases is this disaffection of the lower middle class,” says Julia Ault, an expert on German history at the University of Utah. “Part of their status rests on being better than someone else.” Lower-middle-class Germans in 1930 might have felt a loss of status if they perceived Jews to be advancing more quickly than they were. Ault sees a parallel to what some white people in rural America feel: They perceive immigrants as coming in and rising more quickly than they are.
Rather than a drastic Nazi-style crackdown on free speech, what is alarming many scholars today is the idea of a
post-truth world
, in which
evidence doesn’t matter
if a story reinforces your beliefs.
“In some sense every scholar is at risk,” says Robbert Dijkgraaf, the current director of the Institute for Advanced Study, which attracted many of the scientists and mathematicians who fled Göttingen and other German universities in the 1930s. “It’s not so much that people are persecuted because of their beliefs, but there is a certain trend where careful reasoning, the search for truth, all the delicacies of having a balanced point of view, acting on facts, being honest about what you do and don’t know, your uncertainty, all these values we have in science and scholarship are at risk.”
The dismissal of experts and the appeals to populism are dangerous, says Ault. “It’s going to be hugely devastating to the EPA, to climate science.” Trump, who
has called climate change a Chinese hoax
, has asked for the names of scientists who study global warming. His transition team
backpedaled on the request

unsettling for employees
of the Department of Energy. More recently, it was reported that his administration

• **对历史事件后续影响的讨论**：achenet提到Hilbert对 Göttingen数学研究所因犹太人离开而遭受损失的回应，突显了纳粹政策对学术机构的毁灭性影响。

• **对Operation Paperclip的提及**：dirtyhippiefree指出二战后美国对德国科学家的招募行动，揭示了历史事件的复杂后续影响。

• **对未来政治局势的担忧**：holtkam2对特朗普连任的可能性表示担忧，并质疑为何大多数人假设其任期仅为四年，提出了对权力交接的疑虑。

• **对当代学术腐败的批评**：photochemsyn将历史事件与当代美国学术腐败联系起来，指出自1980年代以来大学研究的商业化导致的欺诈和不信任问题。

• **对当前学术界移民潮的担忧**：iterance提到其学术同行中有人考虑移民，反映了当前学术界职业前景的不确定性和对未来的忧虑。

补充讨论：
• **历史与当代的对比与警示**：许多评论将历史事件与当代社会和学术界的问题进行对比，警示当前学术自由和独立性可能面临的威胁。

• **个人经历与历史事件的交织**：评论中既有对历史事件的分析，也有个人和当代学术界人士的经历和反思，提供了多角度的讨论。

data.title: IBM orders US sales to locate near customers, RTO for cloud staff, DEI purge
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: IBM正在要求美国销售员工每周至少三天在客户所在地、旗舰办公室或销售中心工作，作为“重返客户”计划的一部分。同时，所有美国云部门员工也被要求每周至少三天返回指定战略地点的办公室工作。此举被一些现任和前任员工视为变相裁员，因为年长且薪酬较高的员工可能不愿搬迁，而年轻的早期职业员工更可能接受。IBM还计划在2026年将位于达拉斯的数字销售中心迁至奥斯汀。此外，IBM正加大在印度的招聘力度，同时削弱其多元化、公平和包容（DEI）计划的重视程度。管理层将在5月初与团队讨论具体安排，6月初确定团队的共置决定。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IBM的DEI政策、回归办公室（RTO）政策以及公司历史和现状的争议

不同观点：

IBM orders US sales to locate near customers or offices

'Return to client' push coincides with RTO for cloud staff, DEI purge
Thomas Claburn
Fri 18 Apr 2025
//
00:59 UTC
Exclusive
IBM, which employees wryly or ruefully say stands for I've Been Moved, is once again moving its employees.
On Tuesday, Big Blue shared new rules on where it expects its US sales staff to work: At least three days a week at a client, a flagship office, or a sales hub.
And the mainframe giant last week told all US Cloud employees, sales or otherwise, to return to the office at least three days per week at designated "strategic" locations.
Several current and former IBM employees who have spoken to
The Register
about IBM's work directives argue that these policies represent stealth layoffs because older (and presumably more highly compensated) employees tend to be less willing to uproot their lives, and families where applicable, than the "early professional hires" IBM has been courting
at some legal risk
.
US sales RTO – sorry, RTC
In a staff memo seen by
The Register
, Adam Lawrence, general manager for IBM Americas, billed the return-to-office for most stateside sales personnel as a "return to client initiative."
Citing how "remarkable it is when our teams work side by side" at IBM's swanky Manhattan flagship office,
unveiled
in September 2024, Lawrence added IBM is investing in an Austin, Texas, office to be occupied in 2026.
Whether US sales staff end up working in NYC, Austin, or some other authorized location, Lawrence told them to brace for – deep breath – IBM's "new model" of "effective talent acquisition, deployment, and career progression." We're told that model is "centered on client proximity for those dedicated to specific clients, and anchored on core IBM locations for those dedicated to territories or those in above-market leadership roles."
The program requires most IBM US sales staff "to work at least three days a week from the client location where their assigned territory decision-makers work, a flagship office, or a sales hub." Those residing more than 50 miles from their assigned location will be offered relocation benefits to move. Sales hubs are an option only for those with more than one dedicated account.
IBM presently has five flagship offices for this purpose, one of each in: New York, Austin, Raleigh, Washington DC, and the San Francisco Bay Area. It also has eight sales hubs: Atlanta, Georgia; Boston, Massachusetts; Charlotte, North Carolina; Chicago, Illinois; Columbus, Ohio; Dallas, Texas; Los Angeles, California; and Seattle, Washington. Additional sales hubs may be added later.
Lawrence said Dallas-based workers involved with the Digital Sales center at that location will be moved to Austin in 2026.
The "return to client initiative" applies to sales people associated with US Enterprise, Strategic, and Horizon clients' sites. Those serving US National market territories, Canada, Latin America, US Federal markets, Technology Expert Labs Delivery, Web Methods, and Software Migration Project Office sellers are exempt.
By early May, managers are expected to discuss arrangements with team members; team member colocation decisions are due by early June.
As we
reported
in February, IBM in 2024 began rolling out a co-location/return to office plan that started with managers and has now reached the corporation's broader workforce. Co-location expands on return to office directives by insisting that teams operate out of the same location – it's not enough to work out of any IBM office – and by requiring some workers who have never worked from an office to begin doing so.
IBM shareholders asked to back greater lobbying transparency
Appeals court revives lawsuit alleging IBM bilked pensioners
IBM US cuts may run deeper than feared ‒ and the jobs are heading to India
It looks like IBM is cutting jobs again, with Classic Cloud hit hard
US Cloud RTO and India
IBM's office policy change reached US Cloud employees in an April 10 memo from Alan Peacock, general manager of IBM Cloud. Peacock set a July 1, 2025, deadline for US Cloud employees to work from an office at least three days per week, with relocating workers given until October 1, 2025.
The employee shuffling has been accompanied by
rolling layoffs
in the US, but hiring in India – there are at least 10x as many open IBM jobs in India as there are in any other IBM location, according to the corporation's
career listings
. And earlier this week, IBM
said
it "is setting up a new software lab in Lucknow," India.
DEI'ing inside
This push to hire ever more in India is perhaps what IBM chief human resources officer Nickle LaMoreaux meant in a de-DEI memo earlier this month that equated inclusion with talent acquisition while deemphasizing diversity and equity, the two other elements of DEI.

data.title: The Subjective Charms of Objective-C
data.author: wmlive
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了17世纪博学家莱布尼茨梦想创造一种完美表达所有科学真理的通用语言（characteristica universalis），这一梦想虽未实现，但影响了今天的编程语言。莱布尼茨发明了二进制等，其思想在现代计算机科学中得以延续。作者以自身经历为例，讲述了他对Objective-C语言的特殊情感。尽管这种语言因其冗长和独特语法而备受争议，但在2010年代，它却是开发Mac和iPhone应用的主要工具。作者在大学后期自学Objective-C，通过一本“大黑客牧场”系列书籍掌握了这门语言，并感受到其强大的表达能力。Objective-C源自对象导向编程时代，由Tom Love和Brad Cox创造，因被乔布斯的NeXT公司采用而免于消失，后成为苹果产品核心语言。尽管Objective-C语法复杂，但它提供了一种独特的编程体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Objective-C 及其与 C++、Swift 等语言的比较，以及其在编程历史中的地位和应用情况

不同观点：
• **Objective-C 的优点**：
  - jimbokun 认为 Objective-C 比 C++ 更优雅和强大，尤其是在扩展 C 语言以实现面向对象编程方面。它通过方括号清晰地表达了 SmallTalk 风格的消息传递机制，并且仍然是 C 的超集，能够调用任何遗留代码。
  - VyseofArcadia 也支持 Objective-C，认为它比 C++ 更简洁和合理，尤其是在同一个代码库中通过 Objective-C++ 混合使用时。
  - ramesh31 强调 Objective-C 是唯一的包含头文件的“动态”语言，这使得代理编码工具能够更有效地工作。

• **Objective-C 未广泛传播的原因**：
  - hgs3 对 Objective-C 未能在 NeXT/Apple 生态系统之外流行感到遗憾，认为自由开源软件社区没有采用它是个遗憾。
  - HexDecOctBin 描述了在 Windows 上尝试使用 Objective-C 的困难，指出缺乏轻量级的工作环境，并认为这是其未广泛传播的原因之一。

• **Swift 的崛起与 Objective-C 的衰落**：
  - JKCalhoun 对 Swift 的崛起感到不满，认为 Swift 从各种流行语言中借用特性，导致代码风格不一致。他表示对 Objective-C 被取代感到无奈。
  - mistrial9 批评了对 Objective-C 的偏见，认为其在面向对象编程早期的生存和成功不应被忽视。

• **Objective-C 的历史与应用**：
  - pjmlp 分享了将 Objective-C/OpenGL 移植到 Windows 9X/Visual C++/OpenGL 的经历，反映了 Objective-C 在不同平台上的应用历史。
  - vaxman 详细描述了 Objective-C 在 NeXTStep 和 WebObjects 中的应用及其在企业环境中的潜力，并讨论了其与 Java 的竞争和最终被 Swift 取代的过程。

补充讨论：
• **技术细节与工具支持**：
  - HexDecOctBin 提到了在 Windows 上使用 Objective-C 的具体技术挑战，包括对 libobjc2 的依赖和自定义根类的实现问题。
  - Simplestas 认为 Objective-C 的分布式对象和 XPC 功能非常出色，其他语言无法比拟。

• **个人情感与职业发展**：
  - JKCalhoun 和 markus_zhang 表达了对编程工作的疲惫和对隐退编程生活的向往，反映了部分开发者对技术变迁的复杂情感。

争议焦点：
• **Objective-C 与 Swift 的优劣对比**：部分开发者对 Swift 的崛起持批评态度，认为其风格不一致且缺乏 Objective-C 的优雅，而另一部分开发者则接受 Swift 作为技术进步的自然演变。

总结：
评论中对 Objective-C 的评价褒贬不一，主要集中在对其技术优点、历史应用及其被 Swift 取代的感慨。开发者们对 Objective-C 的技术细节、应用挑战及其在编程历史中的地位进行了深入讨论。

After inventing calculus,
actuarial tables, and the mechanical calculator and coining the phrase “best of all possible worlds,” Gottfried Leibniz still felt his life’s work was incomplete. Since boyhood, the 17th-century polymath had dreamed of creating what he called a
characteristica universalis
—a language that perfectly represented all scientific truths and would render making new discoveries as easy as writing grammatically correct sentences. This “alphabet of human thought” would leave no room for falsehoods or ambiguity, and Leibniz would work on it until the end of his life.
A version of Leibniz’s dream lives on today in programming languages. They don’t represent the totality of the physical and philosophical universe, but instead, the next best thing—the ever-flipping ones and zeroes that make up a computer’s internal state (binary, another Leibniz invention). Computer scientists brave or crazy enough to build new languages chase their own
characteristica universalis
, a system that could allow developers to write code so expressive that it leaves no dark corners for bugs to hide and so self-evident that comments, documentation, and unit tests become unnecessary.
But expressiveness, of course, is as much about personal taste as it is information theory. For me, just as listening to
Countdown to Ecstasy
as a teenager cemented a lifelong affinity for Steely Dan, my taste in programming languages was shaped the most by the first one I learned on my own—Objective-C.
To argue that Objective-C resembles a metaphysically divine language, or even a good language, is like saying Shakespeare is best appreciated in pig latin. Objective-C is, at best, polarizing. Ridiculed for its unrelenting verbosity and peculiar square brackets, it is used only for building Mac and iPhone apps and would have faded into obscurity in the early 1990s had it not been for an unlikely quirk of history. Nevertheless, in my time working as a software engineer in San Francisco in the early 2010s, I repeatedly found myself at dive bars in SoMa or in the comments of HackerNews defending its most cumbersome design choices.
Objective-C came to me when I needed it most. I was a rising college senior and had discovered an interest in computer science too late to major in it. As an adult old enough to drink, I watched teenagers run circles around me in entry-level software engineering classes. Smartphones were just starting to proliferate, but I realized my school didn’t offer any mobile development classes—I had found a niche. I learned Objective-C that summer from a cowboy-themed book series titled
The Big Nerd Ranch
. The first time I wrote code on a big screen and saw it light up pixels on the small screen in my hand, I fell hard for Objective-C. It made me feel the intoxicating power of unlimited self-expression and let me believe I could create whatever I might imagine. I had stumbled across a truly universal language and loved everything about it—until I didn’t.
Twist of Fate
Objective-C came up in the frenzied early days of the object-oriented programming era, and by all accounts, it should have never survived past it. By the 1980s, software projects had grown too large for one person, or even one team, to develop alone. To make collaboration easier, Xerox PARC computer scientist Alan Kay had created object-oriented programming—a paradigm that organized code into reusable “objects” that interact by sending each other “messages.” For instance, a programmer could build a Timer object that could receive messages like start, stop, and readTime. These objects could then be reused across different software programs. In the 1980s, excitement about object-oriented programming was so high that a new language was coming out every few months, and computer scientists argued that we were on the precipice of a “
software industrial revolution
.”
In 1983, Tom Love and Brad Cox, software engineers at International Telephone & Telegraph, combined object-oriented programming with the popular, readable syntax of C programming language to create Objective-C. The pair started a short-lived company to license the language and sell libraries of objects, and before it went belly up they landed the client that would save their creation from falling into obscurity: NeXT, the computer firm Steve Jobs founded after his ouster from Apple. When Jobs triumphantly returned to Apple in 1997, he brought NeXT's operating system—and Objective-C—with him. For the next 17 years, Cox and Love's creation would power the products of the most influential technology company in the world.
I became acquainted with Objective-C a decade and a half later. I saw how objects and messages take on a sentence-like structure, punctuated by square brackets, like [self.timer increaseByNumberOfSeconds:60]. These were not curt, Hemingwayesque sentences, but long, floral, Proustian ones, syntactically complex and evoking vivid imagery with functio

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应在Java中引入运算符重载

不同观点：
• **支持引入运算符重载**：
   - **senkora** 认为运算符重载可以使某些类型的库设计更加优雅。
   - 举例说明C++允许运算符重载，而Java不允许，这是一种遗憾。
   - 暗示运算符重载可以增强代码的可读性和库的可用性。

• **反对或未引入运算符重载**：
   - **隐含观点**：Java在设计时决定不引入运算符重载，表明语言设计者（如Guy Steele）可能认为保持简单性和一致性更为重要。
   - 可能出于对复杂性、可维护性以及潜在的滥用问题的考虑，Java选择不支持运算符重载。

补充讨论：
• **Guy Steele的角色**：ColinWright提到Guy Steele是1998年ACM OOPSLA会议的主题演讲者，暗示他在编程语言设计方面的影响力，可能在Java的设计决策中起到了一定作用。
• **运算符与方法重载的区别**：Java虽然不支持运算符重载，但支持方法重载，这可能是为了在灵活性和复杂性之间找到一个平衡点。
• **争议焦点**：运算符重载在Java中的缺失是否是一个应被改变的缺陷，支持者认为它能提升设计质量，而反对者可能担忧其带来的复杂性和潜在问题。

这个讨论反映了对编程语言特性在设计灵活性和复杂性之间的权衡的不同看法。

data.title: Zig and GPUs
data.author: Cloudef
data.article_summary:
本文简要介绍了使用Zig语言进行GPU编程的现状，包括通过Vulkan、OpenCL和原生ISA进行GPU编程的支持情况。Zig可以通过自托管的SPIR-V后端生成SPIR-V中间代码，并通过LLVM生成PTX（NVIDIA）和AMDGCN（AMD）原生二进制代码。这使得开发者无需使用CUDA、HIP或HLSL即可编写高性能GPU代码。

文章比较了Vulkan和OpenCL在功能上的差异，指出OpenCL允许指针运算和类型转换，而Vulkan限制更多。Zig在SPIR-V后端开发中面临的主要挑战之一是需要明确指定地址空间，而Vulkan不支持某些指令的精确舍入。

未来计划包括增加行为测试的通过率，提供CUDA/HIP运行时绑定，以及扩展标准库中的常见算法以支持GPU运算。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPU编程中不同工具和库的选择，特别是在专业环境下的可行性和兼容性。

不同观点：
• SomaticPirate认为，尽管业余爱好者开发的库（如Vulkan和OpenGL）很不错，但在专业环境中，C/C++仍然是默认选择。他指出，真正的性能提升依赖于特定厂商的工具包（如CUDA、Metal），因为包装厂商提供的框架可能会失效，这对于专业开发者来说是不可持续的。

• skywal_l作为一个GPU新手，提出了关于AMD GPU架构的问题，询问是否可以在新一代的RDNA架构上运行为旧的AMDGCN架构生成的二进制文件。他还对GPU指令集的专有性质表示担忧，质疑二进制生成的可靠性。

• LegNeato提供了Rust-GPU和Rust-CUDA项目的链接，暗示这些项目可能提供了一种在GPU编程中使用Rust的替代方案，从而扩展了讨论的范围，提到了Rust在GPU编程中的潜力。

补充讨论：
- SomaticPirate强调了在专业环境中对稳定性和长期支持的需求，认为厂商提供的工具包更可靠。
- skywal_l关注的是不同GPU架构之间的兼容性问题，特别是旧架构上的二进制文件是否能在新架构上运行。
- LegNeato提供的信息暗示了Rust在GPU编程中的新兴角色，可能为寻求替代方案的开发者提供了新的方向。

争议焦点：
- 主要争议在于是否依赖厂商提供的专用工具包（如CUDA、Metal）以获得最佳性能和稳定性，还是探索新兴的开源或社区驱动的项目（如Rust-GPU）。
- GPU架构的兼容性问题也是讨论中的一个关键点，尤其是在跨代硬件上运行的可行性。

43726413.article_content:
Ali Cheraghi
Zig and GPUs
GPU programming used to mean wrangling C++ compilers, bloated SDKs, and vendor-specific toolchains. That’s changing. You can now write GPU code in modern languages like
Rust
and
Zig
with fewer layers. This post walks through the current state of Zig’s GPU backends and how they stack up across Vulkan, OpenCL, and native ISAs.
SPIR-V, PTX and AMDGCN
Zig’s GPU backend support has been steadily evolving. After
roughly 4 years
, the self-hosted SPIR-V backend is now mature enough to experiment with and port basic shaders and compute kernels. In case you don’t know, SPIR-V is an intermediate typed IR used by Vulkan, OpenCL, and
soon DirectX
. Zig can also use
LLVM
to directly generate PTX (NVIDIA) and AMDGCN (AMD) code, producing native binaries that can be loaded at runtime. This opens the door to writing high-performance GPU code without needing to touch CUDA, HIP, or HLSL.
// SPIR-V:
//     zig build-obj -target spirv64-vulkan-none -mcpu vulkan_v1_2+int64 \
//     -ofmt=spirv -fno-llvm kernel.zig
//     zig build-obj -target spirv64-opencl-none -mcpu opencl_v2+int64 \
//     -ofmt=spirv -fno-llvm kernel.zig
//
// PTX:
//     zig build-lib -dynamic -target nvptx64-cuda-none -mcpu <gpu-model> \
//     -femit-asm -fno-allow-shlib-undefined -fno-compiler-rt -fno-ubsan-rt kernel.zig
//
// AMDGCN:
//     zig build-lib -dynamic -target amdgcn-amdhsa-none -mcpu <gpu-model> \
//     -fno-allow-shlib-undefined -fno-compiler-rt -fno-ubsan-rt kernel.zig
//
export
fn
kernel
(
)
callconv
(
.
kernel
)
void
{
}
For a complete example, checkout
snektron/shallenge
.
Vulkan vs. OpenCL
Today, Vulkan and OpenCL are the two major SPIR-V environments — but they diverge in a few aspects. in OpenCL, capabilities like
Kernel
and
Addresses
are guaranteed to be available. As a result, pointer arithmetic and casting are permitted. Whereas the baseline features for Vulkan and OpenGL environments tend to be more limited. This is why when targeting baseline Vulkan 1.2 features, Zig’s SPIR-V backend passes about
50%
of
Zig’s behavior tests
and
~75%
for the OpenCL target. Note that these numbers are not expected to get significantly higher since a lot of these tests are not meant to be working in GPUs anyway.
Challenges
One core challenge in targeting SPIR-V from a general-purpose language like Zig is the need to explicitly specify address spaces (a.k.a. storage classes). Zig supports this via the
addrspace
keyword, but nearly all Zig code assumes pointers live in the generic address space. That works fine until you need to lower to SPIR-V, where we sometimes rely on
OpPtrCastToGeneric
. Unfortunately, Vulkan doesn’t support that, so as a temporary workaround, all pointers are assumed to be local (
Function
) memory.
Both Vulkan and OpenCL expose hardware-accelerated math instructions via
OpExtInst
, which sometimes can be mapped directly to Zig’s
@builtin
s target-specific instructions when available. However, subtle differences exist. For example, unlike Zig or OpenCL, some Vulkan instructions (
fma
,
sqrt
,
exp
,
log
) do
NOT
guarantee correctly rounded results.
What’s next?
Composite integers
spirv-val
should never fail on a binary emitted by Zig. As Zen says, “Compile errors are better than runtime crashes”.
Increase passing behavior tests.
Provide bindings to CUDA/HIP runtime.
Add or extend a set of common algorithms in stdlib to work under GPUs (prefix sum, reduction, matmul, etc).
You tell!
←
About

主要讨论点：对地球现状的看法及应对方式

不同观点：
• [对地球现状感到绝望，考虑极端应对方式] yo_yo_yo-yo 认为地球当前的状况非常糟糕，已经到了令人绝望的地步。他表示自己有考虑通过开发冷冻睡眠技术（cryosleep）来逃离当前的现实，并希望能够离开地球，寻找新的希望。这种观点反映了一种对未来的悲观情绪和对现实问题的逃避态度。

• [对人类善良和互相关爱的呼吁] 尽管表达了对现实的绝望，yo_yo_yo-yo 仍然在评论末尾向大家送上复活节祝福，并呼吁大家彼此友善。这表明他虽然对大环境感到失望，但仍然希望个人之间能够保持善良和互助的美德。

补充讨论：
• [冷冻睡眠作为未来解决方案的设想] yo_yo_yo-yo 提出的开发冷冻睡眠技术并离开地球的设想，虽然看似是一种科幻式的解决方案，但也反映了一部分人对科技抱有期待，希望通过科技进步来解决当前无法应对的困境。这种想法在科幻作品中常见，但在现实中实现仍面临巨大挑战。

• [争议焦点] 评论中虽然没有直接的争议，但潜在的争议焦点可能在于人类是否应该通过科技手段（如冷冻睡眠或太空移民）来逃避地球问题，还是应该集中精力解决当前地球上的环境和社会问题。这种讨论涉及对科技进步与社会责任之间关系的思考。

总结：评论主要反映了对地球现状的悲观情绪，并提出了一种科幻式的逃避方案，同时不忘呼吁人类之间的善良和互助。潜在的争议在于人类应通过科技逃避问题还是面对和解决现实困境。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一本即将发布的书籍，该书解释了我们日常使用的技术背后的原理，如触摸屏如何感知触摸、高斯模糊的原理、贝塞尔曲线在设计软件中的应用、屏幕像素化及反锯齿等。书中包含大量图片和图表，适合好奇但不一定具备技术背景的读者。它不是教程，不会直接帮助你成为更好的设计师或程序员，但能加深你对技术的理解。书籍初期为数字版，可能后续推出印刷版，读者可以参与预订并影响部分内容的选择。

不同观点：
• [积极评价] 一些评论者对书的审美和设计表示赞赏。例如，[tenacious_tuna]将其与童年喜爱的书籍《The Way Things Work》相比较，[Apfel]对登录页的美学表示赞赏，并表示愿意预订。[thallavajhula]则特别提到邮件列表注册过程的美学体验。
• [功能建议] [georgewsinger]建议作者添加关于如何制作书中精美图表的元条目。[vivzkestrel]提出增加具体技术主题的建议，如微处理器、存储类型和操作系统相关内容。
• [争议与混淆] [felipemesquita]指出副标题与描述之间的矛盾，即书声称是为设计和构建软件的人编写的，但却说无需技术背景。[croemer]则对内容的可访问性感到困惑，认为可能只是个公告。[XCSme]对软件相关标题与硬件图表的搭配感到不解。
• [技术细节] [robocat]纠正了书中关于触摸屏的描述，指出应为电场而非磁场。[pflanze]对硬盘盘片移动方向的准确性提出质疑。[kmoser]希望书中提到的高斯模糊能链接到维基百科相关条目。
• [批评] [kookamamie]认为书的外观酷炫但内容不足。[clausz]质疑书的出版时间，指出版权日期为1990年，可能过时。

补充讨论：
• [工具与制作] [pier25]对书中动画的制作工具表示好奇，推测可能是通过某些工具创作的SVG动画。
• [怀旧与期望] [tenacious_tuna]表达了对类似童年读物的成人版的长久期待，反映出对这种形式书籍的需求。

这些观点反映了读者对书籍内容、设计、技术准确性及其实用性的多方面关注。

1986
Have you ever wondered how a touch screen knows you are touching it? Well, it has these layers of transparent metal electrodes embedded in the display. When your finger gets close to the screen it causes a disturbance in the magnetic field that the electrodes sense.
FIG_
002
Because the electrodes are laid out on a grid, they can report back the x and y co-ordinates of the disturbance to the operating system. Pretty neat.
Or maybe you’ve wondered why we call it a Gaussian blur? When we blur an image, we look at all the neighbouring pixels and multiply them by a matrix of weights called a kernel.
FIG_
003
The most common type of kernel has a gaussian distribution, meaning it gets stronger towards the middle and weaker at the edges. This produces a more realistic blur without being too computationally expensive.
Maybe you’ve always wanted to know how the pen tool works in Figma and what those handles actually do when you move them.
t =
FIG_
004
They control the points on a bezier curve which is a cool piece of math we use to draw curves in vector graphics, like fonts and SVGs.
But of course, our screens are made of pixels and struggle to display smooth curves. So we have to take these curves and figure out how to display them so that they represent the shapes as accurately as possible.
FIG_
005
This is called rasterisation but it’s not as simple as it seems and we need a whole bunch of clever tricks like, anti-aliasing to trick our eyes into thinking we are looking at straight lines.
If you’ve ever wondered about any of these things or if they’ve sparked your curiosity, then this is for you.
This book won’t teach you how to actually make software - it’s not a tutorial or a guide but rather something more interesting than that. It’s a manual that explains how the things you use everyday actually work.
As everything around us has become more complicated our understanding of technology has diminished. It used to be that we needed to understand our tools deeply but today we understand them in a shallow, abstracted way.
It won’t make you a better designer or programmer tomorrow - there’s nothing actionable in here. But knowing how things work comes in handy when you find yourself out of your depth. Or at the very least, you can pretend to be smart in front of your friends.
You don’t need to be technical to read this - there are a lot of pictures and diagrams to do the heavy lifting. You just need to be curious.
MAKING SOFTWARE

data.title: Differentiable Programming from Scratch
data.author: sksxihve
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了可微编程（Differentiable Programming）的基础及其广泛应用。可微编程不仅在机器学习框架如TensorFlow、PyTorch和JAX中流行，还在计算机图形学、可微渲染、可微物理和神经表示等领域得到应用。文章首先回顾了微积分中的导数定义，并解释了导数如何表示函数在小范围内的变化。在多维空间中，导数被视为将域中的向量映射到值域中的向量的工具。文章详细介绍了偏导数和梯度的概念，并解释了梯度如何表示函数增长最快的方向，即“最陡上升方向”。此外，文章还讨论了方向导数的概念，并扩展到多输入多输出函数的情况。最后，文章强调了自动微分在可微编程中的重要性，包括前向模式和反向模式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自动微分（autodiff）技术的背景、应用及其在编程中的实现。

不同观点：
• [FilosofumRex] 认为可微编程（differentiable programming）在20世纪90年代曾是鲜为人知的技术，主要用于工程师模拟如核能和化学等数值刚性系统，随后消失近30年，直到被机器学习/人工智能研究人员重新发现。这表明该技术有历史应用背景，但一度被遗忘，直到近期才重获关注。

• [constantcrying] 指出有限差分法（finite differences）存在重大问题：只能计算单一方向的导数。在高维输入情况下，计算整个梯度变得计算上不可行，因为需要为每个维度单独评估函数f。此外，数值上非常不稳定，f(x)和f(x+h)非常相似，h非常小，容易发生破坏性抵消。不过，对于黑盒函数，有限差分法仍是唯一实际的选择，可以通过双向导数计算稍作改进。

• [weinzierl] 对纯函数（pure functions）在自动微分中的重要性提出质疑。他认为，虽然很多文献强调纯函数是自动微分的关键，但实际中很多函数并非处处可微。他质疑现代自动微分库对输入函数的具体要求，以及为何大家如此关注纯函数性质，而忽略了其他更重要的问题。

• [hwpythonner] 对自动微分与函数式编程语言（如ML和Clojure）的联系表示好奇。他认为自动微分的表达式结构和评估规则与函数式语言相似，并质疑为何需要专门的自定义领域特定语言（DSL），因为现有的函数式语言似乎也能支持类似功能。

补充讨论：
• 自动微分技术的应用历史与重新发现。
• 有限差分法在高维计算中的局限性及其数值稳定性问题。
• 自动微分中纯函数的重要性及其实际应用中的要求。
• 自动微分与函数式编程语言之间的关系及自定义DSL的必要性。

争议焦点：自动微分中纯函数的重要性以及是否需要专门的自定义DSL，还是可以利用现有函数式编程语言实现类似功能。

Differentiable Programming from Scratch
Differentiable programming
has become a hot research topic, and not only due to the popularity of machine learning frameworks like TensorFlow, PyTorch, and JAX. Many fields apart from machine learning are finding differentiable programming to be a useful tool for solving optimization problems. In computer graphics, differentiable
rendering
, differentiable
physics
, and
neural representations
are all gaining popularity.
This article received an honorable mention in 3Blue1Brown’s
Summer of Math Exposition 2
!

Prerequisites
Differentiation
It all starts with the definition you learn in calculus class:
\[
f^{\prime}(x) = \lim_{h\rightarrow 0} \frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}
\]
In other words, the derivative computes how much $$f(x)$$ changes when $$x$$ is perturbed by an infinitesimal amount. If $$f$$ is a one-dimensional function from $$\mathbb{R} \mapsto \mathbb{R}$$, the derivative $$f^{\prime}(x)$$ returns the slope of the graph of $$f$$ at $$x$$.
However, there’s another perspective that provides better intuition in higher dimensions. If we think of $$f$$ as a map from points in its domain to points in its range, we can think of $$f^{\prime}(x)$$ as a map from
vectors
based at $$x$$ to
vectors
based at $$f(x)$$.
One-to-One
In 1D, this distinction is a bit subtle, as a 1D “vector” is just a single number. Still, evaluating $$f^{\prime}(x)$$ shows us how a vector placed at $$x$$ is scaled when transformed by $$f$$. That’s just the slope of $$f$$ at $$x$$.
Many-to-One
If we consider a function $$g(x,y) : \mathbb{R}^2 \mapsto \mathbb{R}$$ (two inputs, one output), this perspective will become clearer. We can differentiate $$g$$ with respect to any particular input, known as a partial derivative:
\[
g_x(x,y) = \lim_{h\rightarrow0} \frac{g(x+h,y) - g(x,y)}{h}
\]
The function $$g_x$$ computes the change in $$g$$ given a change in $$x$$. By combining $$g_x$$ with the corresponding $$g_y$$, we produce the
gradient
of $$g$$:
\[
\nabla g(x,y) = \begin{bmatrix}g_x(x,y) & g_y(x,y)\end{bmatrix}
\]
That is, $$\nabla g(x,y)$$ tells us how $$g$$ changes if we change either $$x$$ or $$y$$. If we multiply $$\nabla g(x,y)$$ with a column vector of differences $$\Delta x,\Delta y$$, we’ll get their combined effect on $$g$$:
\[
\nabla g(x,y) \begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{bmatrix} = \Delta xg_x(x,y) + \Delta yg_y(x,y)
\]
It’s tempting to think of the gradient as just another vector. However, it’s often useful to think of the gradient as a
higher-order function
: $$\nabla g$$ is a function that, when evaluated at $$x,y$$, gives us
another function
that transforms
vectors
based at $$x,y$$ to
vectors
based at $$g(x,y)$$.
It just so happens that the function returned by our gradient is linear, so it can be represented as a matrix multiplication.
The gradient is typically explained as the “direction of steepest ascent.” Why is that? When we evaluate the gradient at a point $$x,y$$ and a vector $$\Delta x, \Delta y$$, the result is a change in the output of $$g$$. If we
maximize
the change in $$g$$ with respect to the input vector, we’ll get the direction that makes the output increase the fastest.
Since the gradient function is just a product with $$\begin{bmatrix}g_x(x,y) & g_y(x,y)\end{bmatrix}$$, the direction $$\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x & \Delta y\end{bmatrix}$$ that maximizes the result is easy to find: it’s parallel to $$\begin{bmatrix}g_x(x,y) & g_y(x,y)\end{bmatrix}$$. That means the gradient vector is, in fact, the direction of steepest ascent.
The Directional Derivative
Another important term is the
directional derivative
, which computes the derivative of a function along an arbitrary direction. It is a generalization of the partial derivative, which evaluates the directional derivative along a coordinate axis.
\[
D_{\mathbf{v}}f(x)
\]
Above, we discovered that our “gradient function” could be expressed as a dot product with the gradient vector. That was, actually, the directional derivative:
\[
D_{\mathbf{v}}f(x) = \nabla f(x) \cdot \mathbf{v}
\]
Which again illustrates why the gradient vector is the direction of steepest ascent: it is the $$\mathbf{v}$$ that maximizes the directional derivative. Note that in curved spaces, the “steepest ascent” definition of the gradient still holds, but the directional derivative becomes more complicated than a dot product.
Many-to-Many
For completeness, let’s examine how this perspective extends to vector-valued functions of multiple variables. Consider $$h(x,y) : \mathbb{R}^2 \mapsto \mathbb{R}^2$$ (two inputs, two outputs).
\[
h(x,y) = \begin{bmatrix}h_1(x,y)\\h_2(x,y)\end{bmatrix}
\]
We can take the gradient of each part of $$h$$:
\[
\begin{align*}
\nabla h_1(x,y) &= \begin{bmatrix}h_{1_x}(x,y)& h_{1_y}(x,y)\end{bmatrix} \\
\nabla h_2(x,y) &= \begin{bmatrix}h_{2_x}(x,y)& h

data.article_summary: 《Digital Antiquarian》的文章讲述了Sierra公司经典游戏系列《King's Quest》的终结及其背后的波折，特别是第八部《King's Quest: Mask of Eternity》的开发困境。在公司创始人Ken Williams于1997年离职后，他的妻子、系列创造者Roberta Williams继续工作，但《Mask of Eternity》成为她职业生涯中最艰难的项目。该作尝试从传统点击冒险转变为实时3D引擎，结合动作元素，以吸引现代玩家。然而，技术问题、新管理层的干预和团队变动使得项目困难重重。最终，游戏虽然推出，但因技术缺陷和开发问题饱受诟病，标志着Sierra和《King's Quest》一个时代的结束。

The End of Sierra as We Knew It, Part 2: The Scandal
18

That’s the challenge: giving the public a formula they know and feel comfortable with, but making it different from anything they’ve seen or experienced before.
— Roberta Williams
Although Ken Williams left his office at Sierra On-Line for the last time on November 1, 1997, his wife Roberta Williams stayed on for another year, working on the eighth entry in her iconic
King’s Quest
series.
King’s Quest: Mask of Eternity
turned into the most protracted and tortured project of her long career.
Roberta had long since fallen into a pattern of alternating new
King’s Quest
games with other, original creations. Thus after
Phantasmagoria
shipped in the summer of 1995, it was time for her to begin to sculpt a
King’s Quest VIII
. Yet she was unusually slow to get going in earnest this time around; perhaps she was feeling some of the same sense of exhaustion that her husband was struggling with in a very different professional context. She tinkered with ideas for the better part of a year, during which the fateful acquisition of Sierra by CUC came to pass. By the time a team was finally assembled around her to make
King’s Quest:
Mask of Eternity
in mid-1996, Sierra’s day-to-day operations were teetering on the cusp of enormous changes, not the least of which would be Ken Williams’s dramatically circumscribed authority. To further punctuate the sense of a new era in the offing,
Mask of Eternity
was to be the first
King’s Quest
game ever not to be made in Oakhurst, California; this one would come out of the new offices in Bellevue, Washington. Most members of the team assigned to it were new as well, with the most prominent exception being producer Mark Seibert, who had filled the same role on the hugely successful
King’s Quest VII: The Princeless Bride
and
Phantasmagoria
.
By this point, the lack of any subsequent point-and-click adventure games that had sold in similar numbers to
Phantasmagoria
, from Sierra or anyone else, was sufficient to
raise concerns about the genre’s health
in any thoughtful observer of the state of the industry. Roberta Williams apparently was such an observer, for it was she herself who decided to make
Mask of Eternity
different from all of the
King’s Quest
games that had come before, in order to better meet the desires of contemporary gamers as she understood them. Using Mark Seibert, who had played a lot more of the recent popular non-adventure games than she had, as something of a spirit guide to the new normal, she conceived a
King’s Quest
that would run in a real-time 3D engine, combining her usual focus on storytelling and puzzle-solving with some action elements. The broader goal would be to create a dynamic living world full of emergent potential, rather than another collection of set-piece puzzles linked together by semi-interactive conversations and non-interactive cutscenes. “We didn’t want to make it so you go here and solve a puzzle, then go there to solve a puzzle, then go to a puzzle somewhere else,” she told an early journalist on the scene. “What we really wanted to bring was that sense of going on an adventure, of going on a quest. It’s not just a word in the title. We want you to feel like you’re really doing it.”
Taken in the abstract, her understanding of what she needed to do in order to keep
King’s Quest
relevant wasn’t by any means completely misguided. Yet circumstances almost immediately began to militate against it cohering into a solid, playable game.
SCI
, the venerable adventure engine that had powered the last four
King’s Quest
games and
Phantasmagoria
, along with dozens of other products from Sierra, was totally unsuited for this one. To replace it, the team wound up borrowing a 3D engine that had been developed by Sierra’s subsidiary
Dynamix
with flight simulators in mind. They never were able to fully wrestle it into a form suitable for this application; the finished game remains a festival of jank, sporting
walls that you can literally walk right through
if you hit them just right.
Roberta Williams felt her own authority being gradually undermined as the new order at Sierra, now merely one part of the software arm of CUC, became a fact of life. In the past, she had enjoyed privileges that were granted to none of Sierra’s other designers — such were the benefits of sleeping with the boss, as she herself sometimes joked. She had worked from home most days, emailing her design documents to the people entrusted with implementing them and then supervising their labor only loosely from afar. data.title: Scientists make water-repellent replacement for toxic 'forever chemicals'
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 国际科学家团队研发了一种无毒替代品，用于替代广泛应用但有害健康和环境的全氟烷基物质（PFAS）。PFAS因其独特的防水防油特性被广泛使用，但其难以降解且对环境有害。科学家发现，氟的“体积大”特性可以被无毒的碳氢化合物复制。研究成果发表在《Journal of Colloid and Interface Science》上，展示了如何通过化学合成创造出同样有效且更安全的新化学品。该团队计划与法国和中国的公司合作，将这些研究成果商业化。

Scientists make water-repellent replacement for toxic 'forever chemicals'
by
University of Bristol
Graphical abstract. Credit:
Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
(2025). DOI: 10.1016/j.jcis.2025.03.018
A team of international scientists has invented a substitute for synthetic chemicals, called PFAS (perfluoroalkyl substances), which are widely used in everyday products despite being hazardous to health and the environment.
Until now, it was believed fluorine—the element in such products which forms a highly effective barrier between substances like air and water, making them water repellent—could not easily be replaced because of its
unique properties
.
But scientists from the University of Bristol in the US, Hirosaki University, Japan, and Université Côte d'Azur, France, have discovered that the unique "bulky" attribute of fluorine, which makes it especially good at filling space, can actually be replicated in a different, non-toxic form. The findings are
published
in the
Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
.
Co-lead author Professor Julian Eastoe, from the University of Bristol's School of Chemistry, said, "From fire-fighting foam to furniture, food packaging and cookware, to make-up and toilet tissue, PFAS products are everywhere. Despite the risks to
human health
, and the fact they don't degrade,
perfluoroalkyl substances
persist in the environment, finding an alternative with comparable properties has proven elusive. But after many years of intensive research, we've made a great breakthrough."
The results of their discovery are published in a study which unpacks the chemical structure of PFAS and pinpoints the characteristic "bulkiness" they sought to replicate in a safer form. It also demonstrates how non-fluorinated components, containing only non-toxic carbon and hydrogen, could be equally effective replacements.
Prof Eastoe said, "Through extensive experimentation, it turns out these 'bulky' fragments feature in other common chemical systems like fats and fuels. So we took those principles and created modified chemicals which have these positive attributes and are also much safer.
"Using our specialized laboratories for
chemical synthesis
, we substituted the fluorine in PFAS with certain groups containing only carbon and hydrogen. The whole process has taken about 10 years and the implications are very significant not least because PFAS is used in so many different products and situations."
The researchers now plan on using these principles discovered in the lab to design commercially viable versions of PFAS substitutes.
Co-author Professor Frédéric Guittard, from the Université Côte d'Azur, Nice said, "These new results are of great interest for industrial and
academic researchers
. We are now working with companies in France and China to bring these ideas to market."
More information:
Masanobu Sagisaka et al, New fluorine-free low surface energy surfactants and surfaces,
Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
(2025).
DOI: 10.1016/j.jcis.2025.03.018

data.title: Australia unveils jam-proof quantum tech that's 50 times more accurate than GPS
data.author: joak
data.article_summary: 澳大利亚公司Q-CTRL推出了首个商用量子导航系统，名为“Ironstone Opal”，无需依赖GPS且无法被干扰。该系统利用量子传感器读取地球磁场变化来确定位置，具有高精度和稳定性，比传统GPS（如惯性导航系统）准确50倍。它小巧紧凑，可用于无人机、汽车和飞机等设备。该技术的推出对于国家安全和自动驾驶车辆具有重要意义，特别是在GPS可能被干扰或中断的情况下。测试显示，该系统能完全独立于GPS运行，精度极高。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：量子保证磁导航技术的可行性及准确性

不同观点：
• **ajb的观点**：对该技术是否需要液氮冷却表示关注。ajb提到现有的类似设备（如SQUID）通常需要液氮冷却，并期待是否可能有不需要冷却的创新发明。
• **anenefan的观点**：对磁场用于导航的准确性持怀疑态度，但承认某些动物确实能够利用磁场进行长距离迁徙和归巢。同时，通过引用相关文献和新闻，指出该技术可能过于理想化，但也提到军方支持的项目显示出该技术在追求更高精度方面的潜力。

补充讨论：
• **技术细节**：ajb提到了SQUID（超导量子干涉装置），这是一种对磁场非常敏感的设备，通常需要低温环境来运作。ajb对是否出现不需要液氮冷却的新技术表示好奇。
• **准确性争议**：anenefan对磁场导航的准确性表示怀疑，但引用了文献[1]和[2]，指出量子保证磁导航在某些试验中表现出比战略级惯性导航系统（INS）更高的精度。
• **军方支持**：anenefan提到军方正在开发更精确的导航系统（文献[3]），这表明该技术可能在军事应用中具有重要价值。

争议焦点：
• 磁场导航技术的实际应用可行性和准确性是讨论的主要争议点。anenefan对其准确性持怀疑态度，但承认在特定情况下可能具有高精度。
• 技术实现的物理条件，如是否需要液氮冷却，也是讨论的一个焦点。ajb对现有技术的局限性提出了疑问，并期待更便捷的技术突破。

总结：讨论围绕量子保证磁导航技术的准确性和实现条件展开，一方关注技术细节和实现的可行性，另一方则从实际应用和军方支持的角度进行分析。

Image of Q-CTRL's magnetometer.
Q-CTRL
Australia’s Q-CTRL has announced the first real-world demonstration of its commercially viable quantum navigation system. The system works without Global Positioning Systems (GPS), cannot be jammed, and is already proving to be drastically more accurate than anything else.
This is a big deal as many vehicles worldwide (including planes and cars) rely heavily on GPS for navigation. However, GPS can be jammed, spoofed, or even denied, especially during military conflicts or cyberattacks.
This is a growing concern for national security and autonomous vehicles, which need constant, accurate location da
ta. In fact, according to a
press release
by Q-CTRL, GPS jamming has been shown to disrupt around 1,000 flights every day.
An outage on this scale is estimated to cost the global economy around $1 billion daily. Therefore, finding a reliable backup to GPS is critical, especially for defense and autonomous systems.
Navigation without GPS
To this end, Q-CTRL developed a new system called “Ironstone Opal,” which uses quantum sensors to navigate without GPS. It’s passive (meaning it doesn’t emit signals that could be detected or jammed) and highly accurate.
Instead of relying on satellites,
Q-CTRL’s system
can read the Earth’s magnetic field, which varies slightly depending on location (like a magnetic fingerprint or map). The system can determine where you are by measuring these variations using magnetometers.
This is made possible using the company’s proprietary quantum sensors, which are incredibly sensitive and stable. The system also comes with special AI-based software, which filters out interference like vibrations or electromagnetic noise (what they call “software ruggedization”).
The system is small and compact and could, in theory, be installed in drones or cars and, of course, aircraft.
Q-CTRL ran some live tests on the ground and in the air to validate the technology. As anticipated, they found that it could operate completely independently of GPS.
Moreover, the company reports that its quantum GPS was 50 times more accurate than traditional GPS backup systems (like Inertial Navigation Systems or INS). The systems also delivered navigation precision on par with hitting a bullseye from 1,000 yards.

• **军方支持**：anenefan提到军方正在开发更精确的导航系统（文献[3]），这表明该技术可能在军事应用中具有重要价值。

• 磁场导航技术的实际应用可行性和准确性是讨论的主要争议点。anenefan对其准确性持怀疑态度，但承认在特定情况下可能具有高精度。
• 技术实现的物理条件，如是否需要液氮冷却，也是讨论的一个焦点。ajb对现有技术的局限性提出了疑问，并期待更便捷的技术突破。

总结：讨论围绕量子保证磁导航技术的准确性和实现条件展开，一方关注技术细节和实现的可行性，另一方则从实际应用和军方支持的角度进行分析。

data.title: Still browsing like it's 1999: Fresh tools that keep vintage Macs online, alive
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了尽管年代久远，一些新工具仍在让老式Mac电脑上网和运行。例如，Cameron Kaiser复活了经典Mac OS版的Lynx浏览器（MacLynx），并更新了其他浏览器如TenFourFox和Classilla，以支持老版Mac上网。他还将Mbed-TLS库移植到经典Mac OS，并尝试将SDL 2引入该系统，以支持更多游戏。尽管经典Mac OS与现代系统差异巨大，但开发者仍致力于让其在21世纪保持活力。这些工具使老式Mac在当今互联网时代继续使用，吸引了怀旧和技术爱好者的关注。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

43727081.article_content:
Software
25
Still browsing like it's 1999: Fresh tools that keep vintage Macs online and weirdly alive
25
You can't keep a good OS down
Liam Proven
Tue 15 Apr 2025
//
10:36 UTC
The first Intel-based Mac was 19 years ago, but new versions of apps for both Classic Mac OS and PowerPC Mac OS X still occasionally appear, and we are here for it.
Most recently, some new internet tools emerged for those determined enough to try to get a vintage Mac on the World Wide Web in the 2020s.
First, we thought we'd try to make you feel old. The last new version of Classic Mac OS was 9.2.2, released
December 5, 2001
. Mac OS X 10.0 "Cheetah" had been released in
March that year
, meaning OS X had been out for nine months by the time Mac OS 9.2.2 appeared. Since the Macintosh turned 40 in
January last year
, that means Classic Mac OS was around for about 17 years. What's now called just macOS is 24, older than Classic ever got. Even the Intel Macs
first appeared
19 years ago.
And yet, some people still run pre-Intel Macs, and even pre-PowerPC Macs. If you do and you want to get online, then Cameron Kaiser of
Floodgap Systems
is a valuable ally. His retro computing interests are broad, and we've mentioned him a few times on
The Register
, such as his deep dive into the revolutionary
Canon Cat computer
, and his evaluation of
RISC-V hardware performance
.
Back in 2020, he
revived
the native Classic Mac OS port of the Lynx web browser,
MacLynx
. Earlier this month, he came back to it and has updated it again, including adding native Mac OS dialog boxes. His account is – as usual –
long and detailed
but it's an interesting read.
He also maintains some other web browsers for elderly Macs, including
TenFourFox
for Mac OS X 10.4 and
Classilla
for Mac OS 8.6 and 9.x.
Back in 2021,
The Reg
reported the end of TenFourFox
. What Kaiser actually
said at the time
was that he was placing the project in what he called "hobby mode":
The browser will be a hobby I purely maintain for myself, with no concessions, no version tags (rolling release only), no beta test period and no regular schedule. You can still use it, but if you want to do so, you will be responsible for building the browser yourself…
Well, if you know how to do that, then you may want to know that
back on St Valentine's Day
he pushed a new release to GitHub. You will need to pull the source code
from his repository
and build it, but a new version is worth having.
The LittleGP-30: A tiny recreation of a very big deal from the 1950s
Pidgin is back, so let's talk about why a local chat client matters
The most important experimental distro you've never heard of gets new project lead
AmigaOS updated in 2025 for some reason
If you're not up to
git pull
commands and elderly Mac OS X build tools, then there is a fork of TenFourFox that may be worth a look,
InterWebPPC
. It's not current with the new batch of patches, but we can still hope for another build.
In other "Classic on the internet" news, although it's not a huge amount of use on its own, there's also a newly released
Classic Mac OS version of Mbed-TLS
on GitHub. This ports the SSL library – also used in the
super-lightweight Dillo browser
– to the older C89/C90 standard, so that it can build in CodeWarrior and run with OpenTransport from Mac OS 9 right back to later versions of Mac OS 7.
Modern macOS
is UNIX® certified
and as such it's not all that dissimilar from other Unix-like OSes, such as Linux and the BSD family. Classic Mac OS is a profoundly different beast, which makes porting modern code to it a complex exercise – but equally, it's a good learning exercise, and we're delighted to see 21st century programmers exploring this 1980s OS.
That may be part of the motivation behind the newly announced and still incomplete
SDL 2 "rough draft"
that appeared a week ago. It builds on the existing
SDL 1.2
port, but so far, it's less complete – for instance, there's no sound support.
"SDL" is short for the
Simple DirectMedia Layer
. It's a
set of libraries
providing a sort of hardware abstraction layer for game development. If "Lauland," the developer of the Classic Mac OS port, can get SDL 2 working well, this could mean a bunch of new games being ported across to Mac OS. ®

data.title: How a Forgotten Battle Created a More Peaceful World
data.author: crescit_eundo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对战争后果的描述及其现实反思，以及对国际秩序和和平的讨论。

不同观点：
• kace91强调战争后的惨状，特别是那些不被广泛展示的、痛苦而漫长的死亡过程，并希望人们永远不要亲身经历这些。
• senthil_rajasek将讨论引向历史上的卡尔inga战争，并提到该战争对阿育王的影响，从而转向对非暴力和佛教传播的讨论。
• fedeb95对文章关于世界变得更加和平的观点提出质疑，指出尽管二战后大国间战争减少，但局部冲突和暴力仍然存在，认为需要更多的规则和外交来防止战争。
• robjwells支持规则基础上的国际秩序，认为如果没有这种秩序，世界可能会更加暴力和混乱。
• KolibriFly补充fedeb95的观点，指出当前的国际规范和秩序其实非常脆弱，依赖于理想主义者的努力和维持。
• begueradj引用诗人Ait Menguellet的话，质疑对战争与和平的简单二分法，并引发对和平来源的深思。
• engels_gibs对“规则基础上的国际秩序”提出强烈批评，认为这种秩序只是西方宣传的工具，并举出美国入侵伊拉克和以色列在加沙的行为作为反例。
• amarcheschi分享了一个关于索尔费里诺桥的历史故事，指出战争的破坏和重建的循环。
• pif认为文章结论有误，强调国际秩序并非由外交官建立，而是由军事研发和国家间的实际权力平衡所决定，特别是提到核武器对国家生存的影响。
• lo_zamoyski详细分析了国际法的脆弱性，指出在主权国家体系下，国际法依赖于各国的共识和遵守。并讨论了美国作为全球霸权在维持自由主义国际秩序中的角色，以及当前该秩序面临的挑战和未来可能的演变。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于国际秩序的有效性和真实性，一部分人认为规则基础上的国际秩序是维持和平的关键，另一部分人则认为这种秩序只是表面文章，无法真正防止战争和暴力。
• 讨论还涉及到对历史事件的不同视角，比如对阿育王和卡尔inga战争的影响的看法，以及对当前国际政治中大国行为的批评。
• 最后，讨论延伸到对未来国际秩序的展望，包括自由主义的衰落和可能的后继者，如古典传统复兴或新的专制主义。

data.title: How refrigeration changed our food
data.author: whocansay
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：冷藏技术、冷冻食品与新鲜食品的比较、现代食品的多样性与美味的丧失

不同观点：
• **冷藏技术的历史与影响**：
  - [userbinator] 指出家用冰箱发明仅约一个世纪，并提到自己对老式冰箱有研究，认为一些老式冰箱仍有历史价值。
  - [theodric] 对文章中提到的冷藏导致食物选择多样性和美味丧失的观点表示怀疑，认为现代的冷藏技术实际上增加了食物的多样性，例如随时可以买到各种水果和海鲜。

• **冷冻食品的质量与新鲜度**：
  - [omnee] 通过在餐厅的体验强调新鲜食材的美味，认为工业化生产和储存方式导致了食物风味的下降。
  - [nottorp] 认为冷冻食品的营养和风味与新鲜食品相近，问题在于工业化种植方式而非储存方式。
  - [ZiiS] 进一步指出，某些冷冻食品（如鱼和豌豆）可能比从市场直接购买的还要新鲜，并解释一些食物风味丧失的原因是未成熟采摘，与冷藏无关。

• **现代食品的多样性与美味的丧失**：
  - [theodric] 不同意文章中关于现代冷藏技术导致食物选择和美味丧失的观点，认为现代超市提供了更多样的选择，且不再受季节限制。
  - [mschuster91] 支持文章观点，认为现代商业化生产的食物品种在风味和营养上确实有所下降，并提到在德国和克罗地亚的农贸市场中可以找到比超市更美味的食材。

补充讨论：
• **具体例子和资源推荐**：
  - [madcaptenor] 推荐了Nicola Twilley的书和其主持的Gastropod播客，提供了更多关于食物科学和历史的讨论。
  - [gnabgib] 提到与冷藏宴会相关的历史讨论，提供了进一步阅读的链接。

争议焦点：
• **冷藏技术对食物多样性和美味的影响**：
  - 一方认为冷藏技术增加了食物多样性，另一方则认为现代食物的风味和营养因工业化生产和储存方式而下降。

• **冷冻食品与新鲜食品的比较**：
  - 部分评论认为冷冻食品在某些情况下可能比新鲜食品更具风味和营养，而另一方强调新鲜食材的优越性。

这些观点展示了关于冷藏技术对现代食品影响的不同看法，并通过具体例子和个人经验支持各自的立场。

data.title: Scientists pioneer chemical process to repurpose rubber waste
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种创新化学方法，用于处理每年大量产生的轮胎橡胶废物。传统方法如热解会产生有害副产物，而新方法通过C–H胺化和聚合物重排，将废弃橡胶分解成可用于制造环氧树脂的材料。该方法由北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校的Aleksandr Zhukhovitskiy博士团队开发，利用硫二亚胺试剂在聚合物链特定位置安装胺基，随后重排聚合物骨架，成功将橡胶的分子量从58,100 g/mol降至约400 g/mol。该过程在温和条件下进行，更加环保和经济，为橡胶回收提供了可持续的替代方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新材料（特别是轮胎材料）的研发及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **ta988的观点**：  
  - 认为使用三氟乙酸（trifluoroacetic acid）涉及大量化学品，而这种化学品由于多种原因令人担忧。  
  - 论据：三氟乙酸作为化学品，在使用中可能带来环境或健康风险，存在潜在问题。

A cleaner future for tires: Scientists pioneer chemical process to repurpose rubber waste
by Dave DeFusco,
University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
Overview of the strategy for rubber deconstruction. a, Proposed route for achieving deconstruction of vulcanized polybutadiene. R is either H, ammonium or hydrated form of aldehyde. b, Mechanism of 2-aza-Cope rearrangement/deconstruction of aminated model polymer. Credit:
Nature
(2025). DOI: 10.1038/s41586-025-08716-6
Every year, millions of tires end up in landfills, creating an environmental crisis with far-reaching consequences. In the United States alone, over 274 million tires were scrapped in 2021, with nearly 20% of them being discarded in landfills. The accumulation of these waste materials presents not only a space issue but also introduces environmental hazards, such as chemical leaching and spontaneous combustion.
While pyrolysis—a process that chemically recycles rubber through high-temperature decomposition—is widely used, it generates harmful byproducts like benzene and dioxins, posing health and environmental risks.
A study titled "Deconstruction of Rubber via C–H Amination and Aza-Cope Rearrangement,"
published
in
Nature
, introduces a novel chemical method for breaking down rubber waste. This technique utilizes C–H amination and a polymer rearrangement strategy to transform discarded rubber into valuable precursors for
epoxy resins
, offering an innovative and sustainable alternative to traditional recycling methods.
The research was led by Dr. Aleksandr Zhukhovitskiy, William R. Kenan, Jr. Fellow and Assistant Professor in the Department of Chemistry at UNC-Chapel Hill.
Rubber, including the synthetic kind used in tires, is composed of polymers cross-linked together into a three-dimensional network that behaves as a tough, flexible material. Recycling these materials is difficult due to the extensive cross-linking within the polymer structure, which gives rubber its durability but also makes it resistant to degradation.
Traditional methods for breaking down rubber focus on two main approaches: devulcanization, which breaks sulfur cross-links but weakens the polymer's mechanical properties; and cleavage of the polymer backbones using oxidative or catalytic methods, which often results in complex, low-value byproducts. Neither approach provides an efficient, scalable solution for repurposing rubber waste.
"Our research seeks to overcome these challenges by developing a method that breaks down rubber into functional materials that possess value even as a mixture," said Dr. Zhukhovitskiy, who is the corresponding author of the study.
The researchers introduced a sulfur diimide reagent to enable the installation of amine groups at specific locations in the polymer chains. This step is crucial because it sets the stage for the subsequent backbone rearrangement. This chemical reaction reorganizes the polymer backbone, breaking down the rubber into soluble amine-functionalized materials that can be used to produce epoxy resins.

The researchers showed that their

works very well. In a test with a model polymer, they broke it down significantly, reducing its molecular weight from 58,100 g/mol to about 400 g/mol. When they applied the method to used rubber, it broke down completely in just six hours, turning it into a soluble material with amine groups that could be used to manufacture broadly useful materials like epoxy resins.
The efficiency of this method is particularly striking when compared to traditional recycling techniques, which often require extreme temperatures or expensive catalysts. The researchers achieved their results under
mild conditions
(35–50°C, or 95–122°F) in aqueous media, making the process more environmentally friendly and cost-effective.

data.title: Ink and Switch Constraint System (2023)
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: 本文总结了relax-pk项目在约束系统方面的进展。在阶段2初期，团队对如何处理约束系统存在不确定性。虽然约束系统具有很大潜力，但以往存在不可靠的问题，如“浮动性”（一个参数变化导致其他参数不自然漂移）、“崩溃”（系统部分操作导致其他部分失稳）和性能不佳。为了解决这些问题，Alex通过传播已知信息和利用线性关系（如y=mx+b）减少了求解器需要处理的变量数量，从而提高了系统的稳定性和性能。团队还引入了“聚类”技术，将约束和变量分组独立求解，提高了收敛速度并为并行化处理提供了可能。最终，多个不稳定结构在新系统中表现稳定，并尝试了多种求解器以优化性能，包括uncmin和g9项目中的改进版。团队计划未来探索更多高性能求解器选项。

title
Constraint System
dated
Fall 2023
author
Summary of work on relax-pk
At the beginning of phase 2, we weren’t sure what to do about constraints. Based on past exploration, constraints seemed to hold a lot of promise but were notoriously unreliable. A good constraint system could unify and power a number of key aspects of the dynamic medium we seek. It would allow for mechanical constructions, like a rope and pulley, that feel physically correct. It would allow for a computational model that bridged between algebraic formulae and tangible objects, like an architectural drawing that changed in response to edits in a parameter table. It’d allow for true bidirectional computation, instead of the limited / biased computation we had in Crosscut.
But constraint systems are hard to implement. They tend to suffer from the following issues:
“Floaty-ness”, where manipulating one parameter causes other parameters to drift in ways that feel unnatural or unrealistic.
“Blow-ups”, where manipulating part of the system causes other parts of the system to collapse inward or explode out to infinity (divergence toward or away from zero, rather than convergence on a reasonable value).
Poor performance, either due to slow convergence or to excess recalculation when constraints are added or removed.
Early in this phase Alex was optimistic that with a bit of effort these issues could be overcome. After a few weeks he was able to show very promising results. This early success built on his earlier work on [
propagation of knowns
] to reduce the number of variables whose values had to be determined by the solver. Then, by leveraging equality constraints (and more generally, any linear relationship between variables —
y=mx+b
where
m
is not zero) he further reduced the number of dimensions that the solver had to worry about.
As an example, consider an angle constraint that “exports” two variables: one whose value is the angle in degrees, and another whose value is in radians. While either or both of those variables may be referenced by other constraints or scrubbed by the user, they collapse to a single variable as far as the solver is concerned — after all, once you know the value of one of them, you can compute the value of the other.
This technique is not just an optimization that enables the solver to converge to a solution more quickly; it often enables the solver to find a solution where it wouldn’t have been able to otherwise. It also improves the feel of our prototype by eliminating the “floaty-ness” that results from duplicated state. More importantly, this technique also enabled us to avoid blow-ups when duplicated or “uneven” constraints are added to a model.
To illustrate this point, suppose the user has added an angle constraint between points
A
and
B
, which introduced a variable
θ
AB
. Now consider what happens when the user adds another angle constraint that involves the same points, but this time in the opposite direction. This is a situation that could lead to an unstable construction. Our new constraint system detects this, and instead of adding the second angle constraint, it introduces the variable
θ
BA
and a linear relationship
θ
BA
= θ
AB
+ π
. So nothing changes for the solver: there is still only one variable (
θ
AB
) to solve for, and only one constraint to satisfy. But to the user, it looks like there are two separate angle constraints. They can further constrain
θ
BA
, or later remove the second angle constraint if they wish. (We are happy to report that all of the
unstable constructions we documented in phase 1
are perfectly stable in our new constraint system.)
Another useful technique we developed for the constraint system is what we call “clustering”, i.e., the partitioning of the constraints and the variables on which they operate into
clusters
that can be solved independently. (As Avi pointed out, this is analogous to the notion of
simulation islands
in some physics engines.) By breaking up the solver’s workload into clusters, we reduced the number of dimensions it has to worry about, which has led to significant improvements in convergence. Clustering also opens up the possibility for us to parallelize the solver — this is something we can explore when we start to build larger projects/models that require better performance.
While these analyses and techniques are an important part of our constraint system, they are not tied to a particular choice of solver. This gives us the freedom to plug in better options as they become available. In addition to Alex’s relaxation-based solver, we tried several gradient descent-based solvers, which resulted in better convergence. The first was the uncmin from
numericjs
. Later, we found a version of uncmin that was modified by Guillermo Webster for his
g9
project, which gave us even better results. We hope to eventually try @Avi Bryant 's new solver which uses auto-diff (instead of numerical differentiation) and WebAssembly for added performance and stability

data.author: ncruces
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了`go-sqlite3`项目中的一个目录`main/libc`，列出了其中的文件和相关文件的最近更新信息。目录包含多个文件，如`benchmark.sh`、`build.sh`、`libc.wasm`、`libc.wat`、`libc_test.go`、`stdlib.h`和`string.h`。这些文件涉及SQLite的WebAssembly支持及其相关的构建和测试脚本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕WebAssembly（WASM）及其相关工具、库和应用场景的讨论

不同观点：
• [cedws] 认为WASM和WIT的文档和术语不够清晰，导致在实际操作中遇到很多问题。他特别提到在构建基本模块时，遇到了需要使用libc的情况，增加了复杂性，并希望有更多的博客或资源来解释这些概念。

• [fuhsnn] 对Wasm内在函数作为高层次固定大小SIMD抽象表示感兴趣，并讨论了其在AOT目标中与库如simd-everywhere结合使用的潜力。他还提到string.h中缺少strstr()函数，并提供了一个替代算法的链接。

• [phickey] 对通过提交更改到上游来加快wasi-libc的速度表示支持，认为这是一种良好的改进方法。

• [forrestthewoods] 对SWAR（SIMD within a register）的概念不了解，提出了基础知识方面的疑问。

• [nu11ptr] 对WASM在多种使用场景中的潜力表示乐观，包括客户端浏览器多语言小程序、服务器端多语言小服务程序、以及语言互操作/外部函数接口（FFI）。他特别指出WASI标准化在解决库调用和调用约定问题上的重要性。

补充讨论：
• WASM和相关工具链（如WIT）的复杂性及文档不足的问题被[cedws]提出，表明需要更多的教育资源和简化。
• [fuhsnn] 和 [phickey] 更关注WASM在性能优化和特定技术实现上的潜力，如SIMD抽象和wasi-libc改进。
• [nu11ptr] 提出WASM在解决跨语言互操作性问题的潜力，尤其是在标准化调用约定和库调用方面，预示着WASM在未来多语言环境中的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 目前关于WASM工具和库的文档和术语复杂性是[cedws]提出的一个主要问题，其他讨论者尚未直接回应这一点，但指出了WASM在不同技术层面的潜力和改进方向。

data.author: kuberwastaken
data.article_summary: 《The Backdooms》是一个受1993年《DOOM》和《The Backrooms》启发的游戏，整个游戏被压缩并嵌入到一个QR码中，可以通过扫描在浏览器中直接运行。该项目展示了极限压缩和QR码存储技术的创新应用，游戏完全离线可用，采用Zlib压缩和Gzip解压缩流，结合Base64编码实现高度压缩。游戏通过自解压网页技术在浏览器内动态解压和执行，用户只需扫描QR码即可立即游玩，无需额外下载或安装。项目使用Python生成QR码，并依赖于`qrcode`和`pillow`库，最终在MIT许可证下开源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个2.4kb大小的HTML游戏《The Backdooms》的技术实现、兼容性及其创意引发的讨论

不同观点：
• **欣赏与赞美**：
  - 多位用户（如[rezmason], [Mainan_Tagonist]）对项目表示赞赏，认为这是一个非常有创意的技术展示，特别是在文件大小限制下的复杂功能实现。
  
• **技术细节讨论**：
  - [teleforce] 提到了在Def Con 32上的类似项目，即在Raspberry Pi Pico 2上运行Doom，将讨论引向不同平台实现类似项目的可行性。
  - [redbell] 表示从该项目中学到了新的技术（'data:' URLs），并提到自己曾考虑过类似项目，但误以为需要HTTP链接。
  - [bananaboy] 对项目描述中关于Doom和光线投射技术的细节提出质疑，指出Doom并未使用光线投射技术，这更类似于Wolfenstein 3D。
  
• **兼容性与改进建议**：
  - [smusamashah] 指出在手机上遇到黑屏问题，建议添加截图或GIF以帮助理解。
  - [giarc] 提到在iPhone上扫描QR码失败，显示“无可用数据”。
  - [jasonjmcghee] 建议更新CSS以使画布显示更清晰，避免模糊。
  - [askvictor] 报告在Android的Firefox移动版上遇到错误，无法完成请求。
  
• **创意扩展与幽默**：
  - [thund] 开玩笑地提出下一个项目可以是将LLM（大型语言模型）作为一个QR码。
  - [Bengalilol] 幽默地表示期待将“自包含的QR码”添加到“CanItRunDoom”网站中，同时调侃这个游戏会让人在扫描QR码时三思。
  - [frellus] 引用小说《Snow Crash》中的情节，幽默地表达对这种技术实现的惊叹和不安。

补充讨论：
• **项目更新**：
  - [kuberwastaken] 自己提到项目更新，增加了对移动设备触摸操作的支持，表明项目仍在不断完善中。
  
• **类似项目对比**：
  - [Barrin92] 提到类似的极小化游戏项目，如.kkrieger，将讨论扩展到其他具有技术挑战性的项目上。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在项目的兼容性问题和一些技术细节的准确性上，如在不同设备和浏览器上的运行效果，以及对Doom和光线投射技术的描述是否准确。

The Backdooms: Running DOOM on a QR Code
Yes, this is literally the entire game. You can
scan it
to play.
🚀 Project Overview
The Backdooms
is a compressed, self-extracting and infinitely generating HTML game inspired by DOOM 1993 and The Backrooms that can be launched and played in a web browser directly from a QR code.
This project was a week-long study I performed (now slightly longer) designed to push the limits of QR code storage and compression, to demonstrate an innovative method of hosting lightweight web applications entirely within a QR code.
Play a slightly less compressed version of this game here
Yes, it's 8bit Undertale Music There
📜 Features
✅
Fully Offline:
No internet connection is required to play the game after scanning the QR code. The URL basically has the ENTIRE code to the game
✅
Extreme Compression:
Utilizes a combination of Zlib compression with Gzip Decompression stream along with base64 encoding to make the final result extremely compressed.
✅
Self-Extracting Webpage:
Uses the
DecompressionStream
API to dynamically decompress and execute the game within the browser.
📦 Installation & Dependencies
Well, technically speaking, just a modern web browser.
But if we do get into the nitty gritty of generating a QR code of a ≈ 2.5kb game:
Prerequisites
Python 3.7+
qrcode
library (for generating QR codes)
pillow
(for QR code image handling)
Install Dependencies
pip install qrcode[pil]
🛠️ Usage
1️⃣ Convert Your Game to a QR Code
Run the script with the following command:
python3 QRGEN.py
<
your-game.html
>
<
output-qrcode.png
>
Example:
python3 QRGEN.py EVEN-SMALLER-SLAMMER-BACKROOMS.html qrcode.png
2️⃣ Scan the QR Code
Use a smartphone or QR scanner to open the game directly in a web browser.
3️⃣ Play Instantly 🎮
Enjoy
The Backdooms
without needing to download or install anything!
🔍 Technical Breakdown
Compression Workflow
flowchart TD
A[Read Input HTML] --> B[Compress with Zlib]
B -->|wbits=15| C[Base64 Encode]
C --> D[Embed in HTML Wrapper]
subgraph browser[Browser Processing]
D --> E[DecompressionStream 'gzip']
E --> F{Format Mismatch}
end
F --> G[Convert to Data URI]
G --> H{Fits QR Code?}
H -->|Yes| I[Generate QR]
H -->|No| J[Reduce HTML Size]
J --> A
Loading
Read Input HTML:
The process starts by reading the given HTML content from a file or input source.
Zlib Compression + GZip decompression:
The HTML is compressed using Zlib and uses Decompressionstream from GZip for best compression
Base64 Encoding:
The compressed data is encoded in Base64, ensuring that it remains text-based and can be embedded in an HTML file safely.
Embedding in HTML Wrapper:
A JavaScript-based self-extracting HTML wrapper is created. This wrapper includes a DecompressionStream API function that automatically decompresses the content when opened in a browser.
Data URI Conversion:
The entire HTML is converted into a data:text/html;base64,... format, allowing it to be stored and shared easily without a physical file.
QR Code Generation Logic
The system first tries to generate the smallest possible QR version using qr.make(fit=True), which dynamically adjusts the QR size based on content length.
If the required version exceeds 40 (the QR code standard limit), it forces version 40 with fit=False.
The lowest error correction level L (which allows the maximum data capacity) is used to fit as much data as possible.
If the data is still too large for QR v40 with level L, the process fails, and an error is returned.
Outcome
If successful, a QR code is generated and displayed.
If not, the process terminates with an error message indicating that the data is too large to be encoded in a QR code.
Understand the Frustration and Trial and Error
Read about the development journey on my blog
MindDump
📜 License
This project is released under the
MIT License
—free to use, modify, and share.
It would make me EXTREMELY happy to see other QR games or even seeing better versions of DOOM in a QR code, given there's so little resources related to this
🙌 Credits
id Software for Developing DOOM
matttkc for putting this idea in my head 5 years ago
Toby Fox for the amazing music in Undertale, this game's GitHub hosted version uses an 8 bit version

We’re hiring our first Customer Success / Sales Engineer, a hybrid role where you'll own the customer journey end-to-end, from onboarding and support to pre-sales technical evaluations. Customer-focused communicator:
Adaptable communicator who clearly explains complex concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
Ownership & initiative:
Self-starter who proactively manages priorities, builds processes, and improves customer experiences.
Sales savvy & product passion:
Skilled at pre-sales engagement and product demonstrations, passionate about democratizing data access.
At Dot, you’ll join a small, but powerful team (currently 6 people) and work directly with the founders, making an immediate and meaningful impact. data.title: How a yacht works: sailboat physics and design
data.author: stass
data.article_summary: 本文概述了翼型、帆船和游艇的空气动力学和工作原理，涵盖升力来源、工程公式、动量理论、升力线理论、环流理论等。讨论了翼、鳍和帆的工作原理，涉及展弦比、洗流、平面形状、边界层、雷诺数等概念。还探讨了风洞实验、下洗、升力槽效应、表观风、风梯度对帆扭曲的影响，以及大船仪器仪表的设置。此外，讨论了附件设计、箔片形状、湿表面积和船体设计，包括摩擦阻力、波阻和弧线设计等。最后，分析了船的整体平衡、稳定性、环境影响和规则效应，以及调校技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：帆船活动及相关技术资源

不同观点：
• **帆船活动类型差异**：jp57指出帆船活动分为竞赛（racer）和巡航（cruiser），并认为尽管两者并非互斥，但竞赛型帆船爱好者往往更关注性能优化，如帆 trim 和各种特殊前帆的使用。相比之下，巡航型帆船爱好者更注重基本的航行技巧，能够在简单的设备下享受航行乐趣。

• **技术资源与设计**：
  - stass 强调了一个专注于帆船和船体设计的网站，该网站包含大量技术资料，如翼型理论、帆扭转、下洗、雷诺数、船体阻力等，并提供了实用计算器和电子表格，是帆船性能建模和游艇设计的宝贵资源。
  - WALoeIII 提到了Arvel Gentry在帆船空气动力学方面的贡献，特别是他对槽隙效应等理论的详细解释。

• **帆船学习与经验积累**：
  - lasermatts 分享了在旧金山发现的两家帆船学校，其中一家还提供造船课程，但因时间和距离问题尚未参加。
  - Zeetah 表达了对帆船的兴趣，但缺乏经验，希望通过志愿服务或参加入门课程（如ASA课程）来获取更多实践经验，并寻求建议。

• **现代帆船技术的发展**：mlhpdx 指出帆船技术的最新进展，如通过新型材料和制造工艺实现的起飞技术（plane on water），以及广泛应用于高端竞赛中的箔片技术。这表明帆船技术已非昔日可比。

补充讨论：
• **帆船历史与文化背景**：contingencies 提到了帆船设计的多种目标（如存储空间、适航性、稳定性等），并讨论了多体船（如双体船、三体船）在速度、舒适性、安全性等方面的优势和成本问题。此外，还分享了关于“catamaran”一词的有趣历史来源。

• **对技术内容的兴趣**：reddit_clone 表示希望看到关于帆船运作的动画解释，以更好地理解帆船原理。

• **其他资源推荐**：boat34189 推荐了一组关于大型船舶建筑、设计、工程和操作的视频，这些资源对中型船只的设计也有参考价值。

• **对网站内容的疑问**：mmooss 对网站创建者Lester Gilbert的身份表示好奇，并寻找相关介绍信息。

争议焦点：
• 帆船活动类型的讨论中，jp57认为竞赛型帆船爱好者的技术讨论对普通巡航者来说过于复杂和不必要，这可能暗示了对帆船活动目的的不同看法。

总结：评论中涉及了帆船活动的不同类型、技术资源、学习经验、现代技术发展、历史文化背景等方面的讨论，展示了帆船爱好者对帆船活动的多样兴趣和深入探索。

43698522.article_summary: 本文概述了翼型、帆船和游艇的空气动力学和工作原理，涵盖升力来源、工程公式、动量理论、升力线理论、环流理论等。讨论了翼、鳍和帆的工作原理，涉及展弦比、洗流、平面形状、边界层、雷诺数等概念。还探讨了风洞实验、下洗、升力槽效应、表观风、风梯度对帆扭曲的影响，以及大船仪器仪表的设置。此外，讨论了附件设计、箔片形状、湿表面积和船体设计，包括摩擦阻力、波阻和弧线设计等。最后，分析了船的整体平衡、稳定性、环境影响和规则效应，以及调校技术。

data.article_summary: Attune 是一个开源的软件制品注册工具，主要用于安全地发布和托管 Linux 软件包，支持 APT 仓库（Debian 和 Ubuntu）。其特点包括灵活部署（自托管或使用托管云基础设施）、安全设计（CLI 本地签署仓库索引，无需暴露签名密钥）和高效性能（增量更新仓库索引）。基本使用步骤包括设置后端服务、安装 CLI、创建和配置软件仓库、添加.deb包、使用GPG密钥签署并部署仓库。该项目采用 Apache-2.0 许可证，主要使用 Rust、Go 和 PLpgSQL 编写。

Attune
Attune is a tool for securely publishing and hosting Linux packages.
Flexible deployment:
Deploy a self-hosted package repository, or use our managed cloud infrastructure.
Secure by design:
Attune's CLI does repository index signing locally, so you can own your signing keys without ever exposing them.
Really, really fast:
Attune does incremental repository index rebuilds, so adding and removing packages is really fast.
We currently support publishing APT (Debian and Ubuntu) repositories, with more
coming soon
.
Quick Start
Here's how to set up an APT repository in about 5 minutes.
Requirements
Docker (
docker
)
GnuPG (
gpg
)
Setup
#
############# First, we need to set up the Attune backend.
#
1. Clone the repository.
git clone git@github.com:attunehq/attune.git
&&
cd
attune
#
2. Set up environment variables by copying from .env.example. You should
#
modify these values as needed to suit your deployment, especially
#
ATTUNE_SECRET.
cp .env.example .env
#
3. Start the control plane and supporting services.
docker compose up -d
#
############# Now, we'll install the CLI and set up a repository.
#
4. Install the Attune CLI by downloading it from GitHub Releases.
#
5. Create a repository.
attune repo create -u
'
http://localhost:9000/debian
'
-d bookworm
#
6. Prepare a `.deb` package to host. One way you can do this is by downloading
#
a sample package e.g. `https://cdn.teleport.dev/teleport_17.4.4_arm64.deb`.
#
7. Add the package to the repository
attune repo pkg -r 1 add -c stable/v17
~
/Downloads/teleport_17.4.4_arm64.deb
#
############# Lastly, we'll use a GPG key to sign and deploy the repository.
#
8. If needed, generate a GPG key.
gpg --generate-key
#
9. Get the key ID of the secret key you'd like to use to sign.
gpg --list-secret-keys
#
10. Export your signing key (replace $KEYID with your key ID, which is the 40
#
character string next to the `sec` entries in each key).
gpg --armor --export-secret-keys --output demo-key.asc
$KEYID
#
11. Sign and deploy the repository.
attune repo -r 1 sync -k demo-key.asc
#
############# Congratulations, you're done!
For more detailed setup instructions and configuration options, refer to the
user guide
.

主要讨论点：Loglan’82及东欧国家在计算机技术发展中的历史和挑战

不同观点：
• tdiff认为Loglan’82是一种超越时代的编程语言，其设计使得程序员无需担心同时代Java程序员面临的许多问题。他还幽默地表示，有时让大语言模型（LLM）写文章可能更好。
• kubb对东欧小国在资源有限情况下，由杰出数学家和工程师推动技术进步的历史表示着迷，并提出如果历史沿着不同路径发展，计算机技术可能会有什么不同的想象。他还提供了一个关于Loglan的研究链接供感兴趣的人参考。
• danielam分享了一个关于MERA-400计算机的YouTube频道，其中包括对其设计者的采访，但指出视频全部是波兰语的。
• mrandish从个人经历出发，描述了在东欧集团国家中，由于中央计划经济和缺乏生态系统，许多工程人才被浪费或未被充分利用。他分享了自己在华沙技术博物馆的经历，指出博物馆主要展示工业、制造和农业技术，计算机部分缺乏英文信息。
• pinewurst补充说明了ODRA 1300s计算机是ICT/ICL 1900的兼容机型，技术上远落后于西方先进水平。
• blogabegonija提到了一部前 cyberpunk 电影《On the Silver Globe》，将讨论引向文化层面。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及东欧国家在计算机技术发展中的挑战和局限，特别是在中央计划经济体制下，技术创新和商业化的困难。
• 评论中也提到了历史和技术发展的平行路径，引发人们对技术进步和历史背景之间关系的思考。
• 提供了关于MERA-400和Loglan’82的进一步资源链接，为感兴趣的读者提供了深入了解的途径。

data.title: The most famous carbon dioxide absorber
data.author: bemmu
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了1970年阿波罗13号登月任务及其意外情况。阿波罗13号原计划是第三次载人登月，但飞行途中发生爆炸，三名宇航员被困在距地球20万英里的太空中。事故后，他们的生存依赖于利用飞船内的有限材料制作二氧化碳吸收器。文章还介绍了阿波罗计划中的飞船结构，包括指挥舱、服务舱和登月舱。按计划，两个宇航员会使用登月舱降落在月球表面并进行探索，但阿波罗13号因事故未能实现登月。最终，宇航员们通过 ingenuity 和团队合作安全返回地球。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apollo 13故事及其相关技术细节，CO2吸收器，技术兼容性问题以及文化趣闻。

不同观点：
• [londons_explore] 提出是否存在家用CO2吸收器，以将室内CO2浓度降至前工业时代水平（约200ppm），而不是城市房屋中常见的800ppm。该评论关注环保和室内空气质量问题。
• [teekert] 认为Apollo 13的故事引人入胜，并建议将其作为“医疗保健互操作性”演讲的引子。此评论侧重于故事的启发性和应用潜力。
• [breakyerself] 指出文章中关于降落伞减速的描述有误，认为应该是热盾首先通过大气层减速。该评论关注技术细节的准确性。
